claims.statement: In French folklore Graoully (also Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille or Graully) is a dragon-like creature that by legend lived in the arena of the Roman amphitheatre at Metz, and Saint Clement of Metz fought and overcame it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Prancis, Graoully (juga Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille, atau Graully) adalah makhluk berwujud naga yang menurut legenda tinggal di arena amfiteater Romawi di Metz, dan Santo Klemens dari Metz melawan serta mengalahkannya.
claims.quote: In French folklore, Graoully (spelled as Graouli, Graouilly, Graouille or Graully) is a creature with the appearance of a dragon. According to legend, it lived in the arena of the Roman amphitheater in Metz, France. Legends state that Saint Clement of Metz fought against Graoully and vanquished the beast.

claims.statement: Serpents in the amphitheatre poisoned the air with their venomous breath and so barred access to the city.
claims.statement_id: Ular-ular di amfiteater meracuni udara dengan napas berbisa sehingga orang tidak bisa memasuki kota.
claims.quote: Mais des serpents installés dans l'amphithéâtre empoisonnent l'air de leur souffle venimeux et interdisent ainsi l'accès à la ville.

claims.statement: The bishop went to the serpents' pit, raised his cross, caught Graoully with his stole, and led the dragon away until it vanished across the River Seille with the other serpents.
claims.statement_id: Sang uskup pergi ke sarang ular, mengangkat salibnya, menangkap Graoully dengan stolanya, lalu menuntun naga itu pergi hingga lenyap di seberang Sungai Seille bersama ular-ular lainnya.
claims.quote: The bishop went to the serpents pit, held up his cross and captured Le Graoully with his stole – the long wide band worn over the shoulders. He then led the dragon away and made sure it disappeared over the Seille River along with the rest of the serpents.

claims.statement: In many depictions and versions, however, Saint Clement instead killed the dragon by piercing it with a polearm.
claims.statement_id: Namun dalam banyak gambaran dan versi, Santo Klemens justru membunuh naga itu dengan menusuknya memakai tombak bergagang panjang.
claims.quote: However, in many depictions and versions of the story, Saint Clément instead slew the dragon by piercing it with a polearm.

claims.statement: According to the German article, on an island in the Seille the monster was swallowed by the earth, and Clement sealed the hole with a rock said still to be visible.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, di sebuah pulau di Seille monster itu ditelan bumi, dan Klemens menutup lubangnya dengan batu yang konon masih terlihat sampai kini.
claims.quote: Dort wurde das Ungeheuer vom Erdboden verschluckt. Clemens verschloss das Loch mit einem Felsen, der angeblich noch heute zu sehen ist.

claims.statement: The word Graoully is believed to come from French grouiller, 'to swarm'.
claims.statement_id: Kata Graoully diyakini berasal dari kata Prancis grouiller, "berkerumun".
claims.quote: It is believed that the word Graoully derives from the French word "grouiller" meaning "swarm".

claims.statement: The German article says the name may come from gräulich, 'horrible'.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Jerman menyebut namanya mungkin dari kata gräulich, "mengerikan".
claims.quote: Der Name soll sich von „gräulich“ (schrecklich) ableiten.

claims.statement: The first version of the legend of Saint Clement of Metz dates from the late 10th century.
claims.statement_id: Versi pertama legenda Santo Klemens dari Metz berasal dari akhir abad ke-10.
claims.quote: La première version de la légende de Saint Clément de Metz date de la fin du Xe siècle.

claims.statement: The legend symbolises the destruction of pagan religions, traditionally shown as serpent and dragon, and their replacement by Christianity.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini melambangkan hancurnya agama pagan, yang biasa digambarkan sebagai ular dan naga, dan penggantiannya oleh agama Kristen.
claims.quote: Cette légende représente symboliquement la destruction des religions païennes — traditionnellement représentées par la figure du serpent et du dragon — et leur remplacement par le christianisme.

claims.statement: A procession with an effigy of the dragon was held in the city until the 19th century.
claims.statement_id: Prosesi dengan patung naga itu diadakan di kota sampai abad ke-19.
claims.quote: A procession with an effigy of the dragon was held in the city until the nineteenth century.

claims.statement: The name of the Rue Taison near the cathedral is traced to a warning about Graoully: 'Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe' (hush, the Graoully is passing).
claims.statement_id: Nama Rue Taison dekat katedral konon berasal dari peringatan tentang Graoully: "Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe" (diamlah, Graoully sedang lewat).
claims.quote: Der Name der Rue Taison, einer Straße unweit der Kathedrale, wird auf eine Warnung vor dem Graoully zurückgeführt: „Taisons, taisons nous, voilà le Graoully qui passe“

claims.statement: A figure of Graoully is in the cathedral crypt, a copy hangs in a hall of the Hohkönigsburg, and until 2021 the beast featured on the crest of FC Metz.
claims.statement_id: Patung Graoully ada di kripta katedral Metz, salinannya tergantung di Hohkönigsburg, dan sampai 2021 makhluk ini muncul di lambang klub sepak bola FC Metz.
claims.quote: Eine Figur des Graoully befindet sich in der Krypta der Kathedrale; eine Kopie davon hängt in einem Saal der Hohkönigsburg. Bis 2021 war das Fabeltier auch auf dem Wappen des Fußballclubs FC Metz zu sehen.

claims.statement: Herensuge is the Basque name for a mythical dragon; dragons appear rarely in Basque mythology, sometimes with seven heads, and Herensuge often also takes the form of a serpent.
claims.statement_id: Herensuge adalah nama naga mitis dalam bahasa Basque; dalam mitologi Basque naga jarang muncul, kadang berkepala tujuh, dan Herensuge sering juga berwujud ular.
claims.quote: Herensuge is the name for a mythical dragon in the Basque language. In Basque mythology, dragons appear sparingly, sometimes with seven heads. Herensuge often also appear in the form of a serpent.

claims.statement: The seven heads were believed to be the Herensuge's offspring; when grown, the little dragons fell off their mother's head.
claims.statement_id: Ketujuh kepala itu dipercaya anak-anak Herensuge; setelah dewasa, naga-naga kecil itu lepas dari kepala induknya.
claims.quote: The seven heads were believed to be the offspring of the Herensuge dragon. When the little dragons were fully grown, they would fall off their mother's head.

claims.statement: Only the god Sugaar is linked with this creature, though more often with a serpent.
claims.statement_id: Hanya dewa Sugaar yang dikaitkan dengan makhluk ini, meski lebih sering dengan ular.
claims.quote: Only the god Sugaar is associated with this creature but more often with a serpent.

claims.statement: According to the German article it is a devilish cave spirit appearing as a serpent, with seven heads and able to fly, though sources differ on this.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, ia roh gua jahat yang muncul berwujud ular, berkepala tujuh, dan dapat terbang, meski sumber berbeda soal ini.
claims.quote: ist in der Folklore des Baskenlands ein teuflischer Höhlengeist, der in der Gestalt einer Schlange erscheint. Der Überlieferung zufolge hat er sieben Köpfe und kann fliegen (die Quellen variieren in dieser Aussage).

claims.statement: With its breath it draws people and animals into its cave to devour them.
claims.statement_id: Dengan napasnya ia menarik manusia dan hewan ke guanya untuk dilahap.
claims.quote: Mit seinem Atem lockt er Menschen und Tiere in seine Höhle, um sie zu verschlingen.

claims.statement: Herensuge lives in caves, mountains and chasms, its attacks terrify shepherds and flocks, and it is at the heart of many heroic tales.
claims.statement_id: Herensuge menghuni gua, gunung, dan jurang, serangannya menakutkan gembala dan ternak, dan ia menjadi pusat banyak kisah kepahlawanan.
claims.quote: Herensuge habite cavernes, montagnes et gouffres, et ses attaques terrifient les bergers et troupeaux ; il est au centre de nombreux récits héroïques.

claims.statement: Its names vary, but the constant suffix suge ('snake') shows its serpent nature.
claims.statement_id: Namanya beragam, tetapi akhiran suge ("ular") yang selalu ada menunjukkan sifatnya sebagai ular.
claims.quote: Ses noms varient, mais la permanence du suffixe « suge » (couleuvre, serpent) suffit à justifier sa nature. C'est en effet un serpent.

claims.statement: Other names include Erensugue, Iraunsuge, Lerensuge, Herainsuge, Errensuge, Edensugue and Igensuge.
claims.statement_id: Nama-nama lainnya antara lain Erensugue, Iraunsuge, Lerensuge, Herainsuge, Errensuge, Edensugue, dan Igensuge.
claims.quote: On trouve les noms de Erensugue, Erensuge, Iraunsuge, Lerensuge, Herainsuge, Errensuge, Hensuge, Edensugue, Edeinsuge, Edaansuge, Igensuge, Iraunsuge.

claims.statement: A legend tells of the Navarrese knight Teodosio de Goñi who, doing penance in the Aralar range for killing both parents, rescues a woman given to the dragon as ransom.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah legenda menceritakan ksatria Navarra Teodosio de Goñi, yang saat menjalani penebusan dosa karena membunuh kedua orang tuanya di Pegunungan Aralar menyelamatkan seorang perempuan yang diserahkan sebagai tebusan kepada naga.
claims.quote: A legend describes a Navarrese knight, Teodosio de Goñi, who while making penance for double parricide in the Aralar Range rescues a woman that had been given as ransom to the dragon.

claims.statement: The knight prays to Saint Michael; the archangel refuses to fight without God, then arrives with God above his head, beheads the dragon and frees Teodosio from his chains and his penance.
claims.statement_id: Ksatria itu berdoa kepada Santo Mikael; sang malaikat agung menolak bertarung tanpa Allah, lalu datang dengan Allah di atas kepalanya, memenggal naga itu, dan membebaskan Teodosio dari rantai serta penebusannya.
claims.quote: the knight prays to Saint Michael to save him. In Heaven, the archangel is notified, but refuses to enter the fight without God. The archangel arrives with God over his head and decapitates the dragon, liberating Teodosio from his chains and ending his penance.

claims.statement: The legend is tied to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar and has been read as justifying the shift from pagan Basque religion to Christianity, especially the cult of St Michael.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini terkait biara San Miguel de Aralar dan ditafsirkan sebagai pembenaran peralihan dari agama pagan Basque ke agama Kristen, khususnya pemujaan Santo Mikael.
claims.quote: This legend is associated to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar. It has been interpreted as a way of justifying the break from the religion and customs of pagan Basques and the adoption of Christianity and, specifically, the veneration for St. Michael.

claims.statement: In the tale of the Grateful Tartalo, a disguised prince kills the seven-headed Herensuge after three battles with the Tartalo's help.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Tartalo yang berterima kasih, seorang pangeran yang menyamar membunuh Herensuge berkepala tujuh setelah tiga kali bertarung dengan bantuan Tartalo.
claims.quote: With the help of the Tartalo, the disguised prince, is able to kill the creature after three battles.

claims.statement: The jentil (Basque plural jentilak) are a race of giants in Basque mythology; the word means 'gentile', from Latin gentilis, and was used for pre-Christian civilisations, especially the builders of megalithic monuments, with which the Mairu (mairuak) are also linked.
claims.statement_id: Jentil (jamak Basque: jentilak) adalah bangsa raksasa dalam mitologi Basque; kata ini berarti "orang kafir", dari bahasa Latin gentilis, dan dipakai untuk peradaban pra-Kristen, khususnya pembangun monumen megalitik, yang juga dikaitkan dengan Mairu (mairuak).
claims.quote: The jentil (or jentilak with the Basque plural), are a race of giants in Basque mythology. This word meaning gentile, from Latin gentilis, was used to refer to pre-Christian civilizations and in particular to the builders of megalithic monuments, to which the other Basque mythical legend the Mairuak are involved too.

claims.statement: The jentil were believed to have lived alongside the Basques; they were hairy and so tall they could walk in the sea and throw rocks from one mountain to another.
claims.statement_id: Jentil dipercaya hidup berdampingan dengan orang Basque; mereka berbulu dan begitu tinggi sehingga dapat berjalan di laut dan melempar batu dari satu gunung ke gunung lain.
claims.quote: The jentil were believed to have lived alongside the Basque people. They were hairy and so tall that they could walk in the sea and throw rocks from one mountain to another.

claims.statement: This stone-throwing explains ancient stone buildings and big isolated rocks, and even the Basque ball game pilota is ascribed to them.
claims.statement_id: Lemparan batu ini menjelaskan bangunan batu kuno dan bongkah batu besar yang terpencil, bahkan permainan bola Basque pilota dikaitkan dengan mereka.
claims.quote: This stone throwing has led to several tales and explanations for ancient stone buildings and large isolated rocks. Even the Basque ball game, pilota, is ascribed to these stone-throwers.

claims.statement: Some credited the jentil with Roland's defeat at Roncevaux, where the Basques beat the Frankish army by hurling rocks.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang mengaitkan kekalahan Roland dalam Pertempuran Roncevaux, ketika orang Basque mengalahkan pasukan Frank dengan melempar batu, dengan para jentil.
claims.quote: Some attributed to the jentil the defeat of Roland in the Battle of Roncevaux, where the Basques defeated the Frankish army by throwing rocks on them.

claims.statement: They were also said to have invented metalworking and the saw, first grown wheat and taught humans to farm.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga dikatakan menemukan pengolahan logam dan gergaji, pertama kali menanam gandum, dan mengajari manusia bertani.
claims.quote: They also were said to have invented metallurgy and the saw and first grew wheat, teaching humans to farm.

claims.statement: They vanished into the earth under a dolmen in the Arratzaren valley in Navarre when a portentous bright cloud, perhaps a star, appeared, heralding the birth of Christ (Kixmi) and the end of the jentil age; other stories say they threw themselves off a mountain.
claims.statement_id: Mereka lenyap ke dalam bumi di bawah sebuah dolmen di lembah Arratzaren, Navarra, ketika muncul awan bercahaya, mungkin bintang, pertanda kelahiran Kristus (Kixmi) dan akhir zaman jentil; kisah lain menyebut mereka menjatuhkan diri dari gunung.
claims.quote: They disappeared into the earth under a dolmen in the Arratzaren valley in Navarra when a portentous luminous cloud – perhaps a star – appeared, said to have heralded the birth of Christ (Kixmi) and the end of the jentil age. Other stories say jentil threw themselves from a mountain.

claims.statement: Only Olentzero remained, a giant who appears at Christmas and is made as straw dolls.
claims.statement_id: Hanya Olentzero yang tersisa, raksasa yang muncul saat Natal dan dibuat sebagai boneka jerami.
claims.quote: Only Olentzero remained, a giant who appears at Christmas and is reproduced as straw dolls.

claims.statement: Dolmens are called jentilarri or jentiletxe, harrespil stone circles jentilbaratz, and caves jentilzulo or jentilkoba.
claims.statement_id: Dolmen disebut jentilarri atau jentiletxe, lingkaran batu harrespil disebut jentilbaratz, dan gua disebut jentilzulo atau jentilkoba.
claims.quote: Dolmens are   jentilarri or jentiletxe, harrespil are jentilbaratz, caves can be jentilzulo or jentilkoba.

claims.statement: In the Basque Country, Bigorre and Couserans about a dozen legends titled 'The End of the Gentiles' tell how a race that preceded present humans vanished in the Pyrenees' golden age.
claims.statement_id: Di negeri Basque, Bigorre, dan Couserans dikenal sekitar selusin legenda berjudul "Akhir Kaum Jentil" tentang lenyapnya bangsa yang mendahului manusia sekarang pada zaman keemasan Pyrenees.
claims.quote: Au Pays basque, mais aussi en Bigorre et en Couserans, on connait une douzaine de légendes avec le titre « La fin des Gentils » qui racontent les circonstances de la disparition d'une « race » qui précéda les humains actuels, à l'âge d'or des Pyrénées.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, the jentilak seem to represent the pre-Christian Basque people themselves, mountain-dwellers par excellence.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, para jentil tampaknya mewakili bangsa Basque pra-Kristen sendiri, penghuni gunung sejati.
claims.quote: Los gentiles parecen representar al propio pueblo vasco precristiano, montañés por excelencia.

claims.statement: The Mairu (plural mairuak), also called Maideak, Mairiak, Saindi Maidi (in Lower Navarre) or Intxisu in the Bidasoa valley, are creatures of Basque mythology.
claims.statement_id: Mairu (jamak: mairuak), juga disebut Maideak, Mairiak, Saindi Maidi (di Navarra Bawah), atau Intxisu di lembah Bidasoa, adalah makhluk mitologi Basque.
claims.quote: Mairu (plural: mairuak), also called Maideak, Mairiak, Saindi Maidi (in Lower Navarre), Intxisu in the Bidasoa valley are creatures of Basque mythology.

claims.statement: The Mairu were giants who built dolmens or harrespil stone circles, found like the dolmens only in the mountains, and are often linked with the lamia.
claims.statement_id: Mairu adalah raksasa pembangun dolmen atau lingkaran batu harrespil yang, seperti dolmen, hanya ada di pegunungan, dan sering dikaitkan dengan lamia.
claims.quote: The Mairu were giants who built dolmens or harrespil. Like the dolmens, they are only found in mountains. They are often associated with lamia, though these are known in all the Basque Country.

claims.statement: Mairu may mean 'Moor' in Basque, used in the sense of 'non-Christian' for former civilisations or megalithic monuments.
claims.statement_id: Mairu mungkin berarti "orang Moor" dalam bahasa Basque, dipakai dalam arti "non-Kristen" untuk peradaban lama atau monumen megalitik.
claims.quote: Mairu could mean "moor" in Basque. This term is used with the sense of 'non-Christian' to refer to former civilizations or megalithic monuments.

claims.statement: The Mairu's origin is thought to be as old as the Portuguese mouros encantados (Spanish moros encantados), considered remnants of old pre-Roman deities.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul Mairu dianggap setua mouros encantados di Portugal (Spanyol: moros encantados), yang dianggap sisa dewa-dewa pra-Romawi.
claims.quote: The origin of the Mairu is thought to be as old as the "mouros encantados" in Portuguese (Spanish: moros encantados), who are thought to be the remnant of old pre-Roman deities.

claims.statement: The Mairuak are credited with building dolmens and cromlechs such as those of Ibañeta at Zugarramurdi, Oiartzun and Buluntza.
claims.statement_id: Mairuak dianggap membangun sejumlah dolmen dan kromlek, seperti di Ibañeta di Zugarramurdi, Oiartzun, dan Buluntza.
claims.quote: On attribue aux Mairuak la construction de certains dolmens et cromlechs comme ceux d'Ibañeta à Zugarramurdi, d'Oiartzun et de Buluntza.

claims.statement: Mairu-baratze, literally 'Mairu's garden', means a small cromlech.
claims.statement_id: Mairu-baratze, harfiah "kebun Mairu", adalah sebutan untuk kromlek kecil.
claims.quote: Mairu-baratze (littéralement 'jardin de Mairu') désigne un petit cromlech.

claims.statement: In some legends Mairu-beso is the dried arm or arm bone of a Mairu with mysterious powers, in practice the arm of an unbaptised newborn.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian legenda, Mairu-beso adalah lengan kering atau tulang lengan Mairu yang berkhasiat gaib, yang sebenarnya lengan bayi yang belum dibaptis.
claims.quote: Dans certaines légendes, Mairu-beso est le bras desséché ou un os du bras de Mairu qui possède des vertus mystérieuses. Plus concrètement, c'est le bras d'un nouveau-né non baptisé.

claims.statement: In the stories the protagonist uses the bone as a torch and sometimes to put the household he has broken into to sleep.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisahnya, tokoh utama memakai tulang itu sebagai obor dan kadang untuk menidurkan penghuni rumah yang dimasukinya.
claims.quote: Dans les narrations, le protagoniste utilise cet os comme torche pour s'éclairer et parfois pour endormir les habitants de la maison dans laquelle il s'est introduit.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the Mairu is a giant or jentil who builds castles, dolmens and other megaliths in Basque mythology.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Mairu adalah raksasa atau jentil yang membangun kastel, dolmen, dan monumen megalitik lain dalam mitologi Basque.
claims.quote: Mairu (Mairuak au pluriel en basque) est un géant ou jentil construisant des châteaux, dolmens et autres monuments mégalithiques dans la mythologie du Pays basque.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, in Oiartzun the builders of the cromlechs are called intxitxu and the cromlechs are said to be their graveyards.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, di Oiartzun para pembangun kromlek disebut intxitxu, dan kromlek itu dikatakan kuburan mereka.
claims.quote: En Oyarzun llaman intxitxu a los constructores de los crómlechs de la región y dicen que son cementerios de estos genios.

claims.statement: The trasgo, trasno or trasgu is a mythological creature in the traditions of several cultures of northern Spain, especially Galician, Asturian and Cantabrian, and also in legends of northern Portugal.
claims.statement_id: Trasgo, trasno, atau trasgu adalah makhluk mitologis dalam tradisi beberapa budaya Spanyol utara, terutama Galisia, Asturias, dan Cantabria, juga dalam legenda Portugal utara.
claims.quote: The trasgo, trasno or trasgu is a mythological creature present in the tradition of several cultures of what is now northern Spain, especially in  Galician, Asturian and Cantabrian traditional culture, it is also found in legends of North Portugal.

claims.statement: It is a mischievous, restless house goblin, often shown as a tiny man limping on his right leg, dark-skinned, in red clothes and a pointed red hat, with a hole in his left hand.
claims.statement_id: Ia peri rumah yang usil dan gelisah, sering digambarkan sebagai lelaki kecil yang pincang kaki kanan, berkulit gelap, berpakaian merah dan bertopi merah runcing, dengan lubang di tangan kirinya.
claims.quote: It is a domestic goblin with a mischievous and nervous character. It is often represented as a tiny man who limps with his right leg; he has dark skin, wears red clothes and a pointy red hat. He has a hole in his left hand.

claims.statement: Night noises and small pranks such as moving objects are blamed on him; he enters homes at night while the household sleeps.
claims.statement_id: Suara-suara malam dan keusilan kecil seperti memindahkan barang dianggap ulahnya; ia masuk ke rumah pada malam hari ketika penghuninya tidur.
claims.quote: Nocturnal noises are attributed to him, and also small pranks like changing the location of objects. He enters homes at night when the inhabitants are asleep.

claims.statement: On the other hand, when treated well, he does the housework at night.
claims.statement_id: Sebaliknya, bila diperlakukan baik, ia mengerjakan pekerjaan rumah pada malam hari.
claims.quote: On the other hand, when he is treated well, he does house chores during the night.

claims.statement: In one tale a household moves away because of the trasgu; on the way the wife asks whether they left anything, and the trasgu, following them, answers: 'You left the lamp, but I'm carrying it.'
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah kisah, penghuni rumah pindah karena trasgu; di jalan sang istri bertanya apakah ada yang tertinggal, dan trasgu yang mengikuti mereka menjawab, "Kalian meninggalkan lampu, tapi aku membawanya."
claims.quote: In a tale, the inhabitants of a house abandoned it because of the trasgu. On their way to the new house, the woman asks her husband: "Have we left anything?" The trasgu, following them, answers: "You have left the lamp, but I'm carrying it."

claims.statement: To get rid of a trasgu one must set him an impossible task, such as carrying sea water in a basket, picking millet off the floor (it falls through the hole in his hand) or whitening a black sheep.
claims.statement_id: Untuk mengusir trasgu ia harus diberi tugas mustahil, seperti membawa air laut dalam keranjang, memungut biji jawawut dari lantai (yang jatuh lewat lubang di tangannya), atau memutihkan domba hitam.
claims.quote: In order to expel a trasgu it is necessary to request of him an impossible task, like bringing a basket of water from the sea, picking up millet from the floor (it falls through the hole in his hand), and whitening a black sheep.

claims.statement: In Asturias the trasgu has different names by place, such as Trasno, Cornín or Xuan Dos Camíos in western Asturias.
claims.statement_id: Di Asturias trasgu punya nama berbeda menurut tempat, seperti Trasno, Cornín, atau Xuan Dos Camíos di Asturias barat.
claims.quote: In Asturias, the trasgu is known by different names depending on the location. He is known as Trasno, Cornín or Xuan Dos Camíos in western Asturias.

claims.statement: The trasgu or trasno is very common in the folklore of Trás-os-Montes and was carried by the Portuguese across their empire, giving rise to similar myths such as the Saci in Brazil.
claims.statement_id: Trasgu atau trasno sangat umum dalam cerita rakyat Trás-os-Montes dan dibawa orang Portugis ke seluruh kekaisaran mereka, melahirkan mitos serupa seperti Saci di Brasil.
claims.quote: Trasgu or trasno (in Galician and Portuguese) is very common in the folklore of Trás-os-Montes and it was taken by the Portuguese throughout their empire originating similar myths like the Saci in Brazil.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, the name comes from Latin transgredī, 'one who transgresses', and in Galicia he is called trasgo, trasno or tardo.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, namanya dari bahasa Latin transgredī, "yang melanggar", dan di Galisia ia disebut trasgo, trasno, atau tardo.
claims.quote: Del latín transgredī ('el que transgrede, el que rompe con la ley')  se le denomina trasgo, trasno o tardo en Galicia

claims.statement: The Russian article also calls the trasgu the best-known being of Asturian mythology, a mischievous, restless house goblin.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Rusia juga menyebut trasgu makhluk paling terkenal dalam mitologi Asturias, peri rumah yang usil dan gelisah.
claims.quote: Тресго наиболее известны в астурийской мифологии. Это домашний гоблин с озорным и нервным характером.

claims.statement: In Catalan mythology an aloja (also dona d'aigua, goja or paitida) is a female being living where there is fresh water, said to be able to turn into a water blackbird (dipper).
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Katalan, aloja (juga dona d'aigua, goja, atau paitida) adalah makhluk perempuan yang tinggal di tempat berair tawar dan konon dapat menjelma menjadi burung air (dipper).
claims.quote: In Catalan mythology an aloja ... also known as dona d'aigua, goja or paitida, is a feminine being that lives in places with fresh water. These "water-women" are said to be able to turn into water blackbirds.

claims.statement: They are not immortal but can live for thousands of years and stay young.
claims.statement_id: Mereka tidak abadi, tetapi dapat hidup ribuan tahun dan tetap muda.
claims.quote: According to legend, these women are not immortal, but can live for thousands of years and retain their youth.

claims.statement: The lakes where they bathe are said to boil with anger if a stranger enters; in Mallorca the most famous is Maria Enganxa, who lives in every well and cistern and hooks children who pass by.
claims.statement_id: Danau tempat mereka mandi konon mendidih karena marah bila orang asing masuk; di Mallorca dona d'aigua paling terkenal adalah Maria Enganxa, yang tinggal di semua sumur dan bak air dan menarik anak yang lewat dengan kaitnya.
claims.quote: It is said that the lakes where the dones d'aigua bathe can boil in anger if any stranger enters them. In Mallorca, the most famous water-woman is Maria Enganxa. According to tradition, she lives inside all the wells and cisterns and takes all the children that pass near them with her hook.

claims.statement: They are nocturnal, with shimmering gold or red hair and emerald or deep blue eyes, wear fine clothes and like to see their reflection in lakes on full-moon nights.
claims.statement_id: Mereka makhluk malam berambut emas atau merah berkilau, bermata hijau zamrud atau biru tua, berpakaian indah, dan suka bercermin di danau pada malam bulan purnama.
claims.quote: According to myth, water-women are nocturnal; have shimmering gold or red hair, and emerald or deep blue eyes; wear fine, rich clothes; and enjoy viewing their reflections in lakes on full-moon nights.

claims.statement: In tales of marriage with humans the condition is often that the husband must not reveal his wife is a water-woman; if he does, she leaves and takes his fortune.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah pernikahan dengan manusia, syaratnya sering bahwa sang suami tidak boleh membocorkan bahwa istrinya dona d'aigua; bila melanggar, ia pergi membawa kekayaannya.
claims.quote: Often, one of the conditions is that the husband cannot reveal that his wife is a water-woman. If he does, the water-woman leaves him and disappears with his fortune.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article they are spirits favouring births and fertility, life-givers and renewers of nature, generally kindly though one should be careful on meeting them.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, mereka roh yang mendukung kelahiran dan kesuburan, pemberi kehidupan dan pemulih alam, umumnya baik hati meski perlu berhati-hati bila bertemu mereka.
claims.quote: Son genios que favorecen los nacimientos y la fertilidad, dadoras de vida y regeneradoras constantes de la naturaleza. Son en general benévolas, aunque debe tenerse prudencia si uno se las encuentra.

claims.statement: The word goja may come from Old Catalan or Occitan, meaning 'young maiden'.
claims.statement_id: Kata goja mungkin berasal dari bahasa Katalan kuno atau Oksitan, berarti "gadis muda".
claims.quote: La palabra «goja» (cat. pl. «goges») podría venir del catalán antiguo o tal vez del occitano, con el significado de 'doncella joven', 'muchacha', 'niña'

claims.statement: They always live near cold blue waters: Pyrenean tarns, torrents and waterfalls, forest springs, pools, damp caves and underground streams and lakes.
claims.statement_id: Mereka selalu tinggal dekat air biru yang dingin: danau Pyrenees, sungai deras dan air terjun, mata air hutan, kolam, gua lembap, dan sungai serta danau bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Habitan siempre cerca de aguas gélidas y azules: los estanques del Pirineo, torrentes y saltos de agua, fuentes de los bosques, pozas, manantiales, grutas húmedas, y corrientes y lagos subterráneos.

claims.statement: They are a local adaptation of the nymphs as embodiments of nature's feminine forces.
claims.statement_id: Mereka adaptasi lokal dari nimfa sebagai perwujudan kekuatan feminin alam.
claims.quote: Son una adaptación local de las ninfas como representaciones de las fuerzas (femeninas) de la naturaleza.

claims.statement: The Aragonese article also says they live in the Pyrenees where there is water, such as springs, rivers, torrents or damp caves.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Aragon juga menyebut mereka tinggal di Pyrenees, di tempat berair seperti mata air, sungai, aliran deras, atau gua lembap.
claims.quote: Viven en os Pireneus, en zonas an bi ha augua, ya sigan fuents, ríos, torrents u espelungas humedas.

claims.statement: Anguane are mythical beings of northern Italian folklore, usually shown as cloven-footed water nymphs with beautiful faces and long breasts.
claims.statement_id: Anguane adalah makhluk mitis cerita rakyat Italia utara yang biasanya digambarkan sebagai nimfa air berkaki belah dengan wajah cantik dan payudara panjang.
claims.quote: Anguane are mythical creatures in Northern Italian folklore, which are traditionally depicted as cloven-footed water nymphs with beautiful faces and long breasts.

claims.statement: They were said to carry their children in baskets on their backs and to fling their breasts over their shoulders to nurse them.
claims.statement_id: Mereka konon menggendong anak dalam keranjang di punggung dan dapat menyampirkan payudaranya ke belakang untuk menyusui anak itu.
claims.quote: They were said to have carried their children in baskets held on their backs, and to have been able to throw their breasts over their backs to nurse these children.

claims.statement: Anguane were thought to live in or near lakes; by myth they seduce male travellers and help barren women conceive.
claims.statement_id: Anguane dipercaya tinggal di dalam atau dekat danau; menurut mitos mereka merayu lelaki pengembara dan membantu perempuan mandul hamil.
claims.quote: Anguane were believed to resided in or nearby lakes. According to myth, Anguane seduce male wayfarers and help infertile women become pregnant.

claims.statement: According to the German article, the anguana (from Latin aqua, 'water'; also Aguana, Guana, Gana, Eguana, Agana, Enguana) is a female spirit of Ladin and Romansh mythology.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, anguana (dari bahasa Latin aqua, "air"; juga Aguana, Guana, Gana, Eguana, Agana, Enguana) adalah makhluk halus perempuan dari mitologi Ladin dan Rumansch.
claims.quote: Als Anguana (von lat. aqua = Wasser; auch Aguana, Guana, Gana, Eguana, Agana, Enguana) bezeichnet man eine Dämonin aus der ladinischen bzw. romanischsprachigen Mythologie

claims.statement: They are said to bring lifelong misfortune if insulted.
claims.statement_id: Konon mereka membawa kemalangan seumur hidup bila dihina.
claims.quote: Es heißt, dass sie ein Leben lang Unglück bringen sollen, wenn man sie beleidigt.

claims.statement: They can appear as beautiful young women or as ugly old women with goat's feet.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dapat muncul sebagai perempuan muda yang cantik atau sebagai perempuan tua buruk rupa berkaki kambing.
claims.quote: Sie können sowohl als schöne, junge, attraktive Frauen, als auch als alte, hässliche Frauen mit Ziegenfüßen in Erscheinung treten.

claims.statement: They supposedly live by brooks, springs or in caves washing linen, and show themselves only at dawn and dusk.
claims.statement_id: Mereka konon tinggal di tepi sungai kecil, mata air, atau gua sambil mencuci kain linen, dan hanya terlihat saat fajar dan senja.
claims.quote: Angeblich leben sie an Bächen, Quellen oder in Höhlen und waschen Leinen. Auch sollen sie sich nur zur Morgen- und Abenddämmerung blicken lassen.

claims.statement: They sometimes marry humans like fairies do, but the husband must not touch their blond hair; they also give 'endless gifts', things that never run out.
claims.statement_id: Kadang mereka menikah dengan manusia seperti peri, tetapi sang suami tidak boleh menyentuh rambut pirangnya; mereka juga memberi "hadiah tanpa akhir", benda yang tak pernah habis.
claims.quote: Zuweilen sollen sie auch Ehen mit den Menschen eingehen, ähnlich wie auch die Feen, allerdings darf der Mann dann nicht ihr blondes Haar berühren. Darüber hinaus sollen sie „unendliche Geschenke“ (also Dinge, die nie zu Ende gehen) überreichen.

claims.statement: In Ladin they are called Gana (singular) or Ganes (plural) for short.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Ladin mereka disebut singkat Gana (tunggal) atau Ganes (jamak).
claims.quote: In der ladinischen Sprache werden sie verkürzt als Gana (Einzahl) oder Ganes (Mehrzahl) bezeichnet.

claims.statement: According to the Italian article, the anguana is a water being somewhat like a nymph, typical of Alpine mythology.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, anguana adalah makhluk air mirip nimfa yang khas mitologi Alpen.
claims.quote: L'anguana è una creatura associata all'acqua, dalle caratteristiche in parte simili a quelle di una ninfa e tipica della mitologia alpina.

claims.statement: According to the Italian article, tales of the anguane (agane in Friulian, Carnic and Dolomite Ladin traditions) are remembered mainly in the foothill and mountain regions.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, kisah anguane (agane dalam tradisi Friuli, Carnia, dan Ladin Dolomit) terutama diingat di daerah kaki gunung dan pegunungan.
claims.quote: Storie sulle anguane (agane nelle tradizioni friulane, carniche e ladine dolomitiche) si ricordano soprattutto nelle regioni pedemontane e montane

claims.statement: Bicorn and Chichevache are fabulous beasts of European satire in the Middle Ages and Renaissance; Bicorn, part panther, part cow with a human face, devours kind and devoted husbands and is fat because they are plentiful.
claims.statement_id: Bicorn dan Chichevache adalah binatang dongeng dalam karya satire Eropa Abad Pertengahan dan Renaisans; Bicorn, setengah macan tutul setengah sapi berwajah manusia, memangsa suami yang baik dan setia sehingga gemuk karena mangsanya melimpah.
claims.quote: Bicorn and Chichevache are fabulous beasts that appear in European satirical works of the Middle Ages and Renaissance. Bicorn is a creature—part panther, part cow, with a human-like face—that devours kind-hearted and devoted husbands and (because of their abundance) is plump and well fed.

claims.statement: Chichevache instead devours obedient wives and is thin and starving because they are scarce.
claims.statement_id: Chichevache sebaliknya memangsa istri yang patuh sehingga kurus kelaparan karena mangsanya langka.
claims.quote: Chichevache, on the other hand, devours obedient wives and (because of their scarcity) is thin and starving.

claims.statement: Geoffrey Chaucer names Chichevache in the envoy of the Clerk's Tale in the Canterbury Tales, ironically warning wives against Griselda's patience and obedience.
claims.statement_id: Geoffrey Chaucer menyebut Chichevache dalam penutup The Clerk's Tale dalam Canterbury Tales, secara ironis memperingatkan para istri agar tidak sesabar dan sepatuh Griselda.
claims.quote: Geoffrey Chaucer mentions Chichevache in the envoy of the Clerk's Tale in his Canterbury Tales, ironically warning wives against the patience and obedience shown by Griselda in the story

claims.statement: Chaucer may have borrowed the French chichifache ('thin face') and blended it with vache ('cow') into chichevache ('thin cow').
claims.statement_id: Chaucer mungkin meminjam istilah Prancis chichifache ("wajah kurus") dan memadukannya dengan vache ("sapi") menjadi chichevache ("sapi kurus").
claims.quote: Chaucer may have borrowed the French term chichifache ("thin face") and blended it with vache ("cow") to make the similar term chichevache ("thin or meagre cow").

claims.statement: In the early 15th century John Lydgate wrote Bycorne and Chychevache, a 133-line poem in 7-line stanzas, probably from a French original.
claims.statement_id: Pada awal abad ke-15 John Lydgate menulis Bycorne and Chychevache, puisi 133 baris dalam bait tujuh baris, mungkin dari karya asli Prancis.
claims.quote: In the early fifteenth century John Lydgate wrote "Bycorne and Chychevache", a 133-line poem in 7-line stanzas, probably from a French original.

claims.statement: Lydgate presents the two beasts as husband and wife.
claims.statement_id: Lydgate menggambarkan kedua binatang itu sebagai suami dan istri.
claims.quote: Lydgate describes the two beasts as husband and wife.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Bigorne and Chicheface are fantastic animals of the folklore of Anjou, Normandy and Auvergne.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Bigorne dan Chicheface adalah binatang khayalan dalam cerita rakyat Anjou, Normandia, dan Auvergne.
claims.quote: Bigorne et Chicheface sont des animaux fantastiques du folklore en Anjou, en Normandie, mais aussi en Auvergne.

claims.statement: Bigorne, which looked like a tiger, was full, fat and sleek because it ate men tyrannised by their wives.
claims.statement_id: Bigorne, yang berwujud seperti harimau, kenyang dan gemuk karena memangsa lelaki yang ditindas istrinya.
claims.quote: Bigorne au contraire, qui  avait l'apparence d'un  tigre, était repu, gros et gras, car il mangeait les hommes tyrannisés par leur femme

claims.statement: In Poitou-Charentes the Bigorne was a fantastic animal that lured and ate small children who came too close to ponds or wells.
claims.statement_id: Di Poitou-Charentes, Bigorne adalah binatang khayalan yang memikat dan memakan anak kecil yang terlalu dekat dengan kolam atau sumur.
claims.quote: La Bigorne dans le Poitou-Charentes était un animal fantastique qui attirait et mangeait les petits enfants qui s'approchaient un peu trop des points d'eau comme les mares, les puits etc.

claims.statement: The Russian article says the Bicorn, besides its two horns, has a body half cow, half panther and a human face.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Rusia menyebut Bicorn, selain bertanduk dua, bertubuh setengah sapi setengah macan tutul dan berwajah manusia.
claims.quote: Двурог, помимо обладания двумя рогами, имеет тело наполовину коровы и наполовину пантеры, а также человеческое лицо.

claims.statement: A bicorn is mentioned in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, its powdered horn an ingredient of Polyjuice Potion.
claims.statement_id: Bicorn disebut dalam Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets, dan bubuk tanduknya menjadi bahan Ramuan Polijus.
claims.quote: A bicorn is mentioned in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets. Its powdered horn is used as an ingredient in Polyjuice Potion.

claims.statement: The Căpcăun is a creature of Romanian folklore, an ogre who kidnaps children or young ladies, mostly princesses, and embodies evil like the Zmeu and the Balaur.
claims.statement_id: Căpcăun adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Rumania, raksasa pemakan manusia yang menculik anak atau gadis muda, terutama putri raja, dan melambangkan kejahatan seperti Zmeu dan Balaur.
claims.quote: A Căpcăun is a creature in Romanian folklore, depicted as an ogre who kidnaps children or young ladies (mostly princesses). It represents evil, as do its counterparts Zmeu and the Balaur.

claims.statement: The Romanian word seems to mean 'dog-head' (căp from cap, 'head', and căun from câine, 'dog'); the căpcăun has a dog's head, sometimes four eyes, eyes in the nape or four legs, and its main trait is cannibalism.
claims.statement_id: Kata Rumania ini tampaknya berarti "kepala anjing" (căp dari cap, "kepala", dan căun dari câine, "anjing"); căpcăun berkepala anjing, kadang bermata empat, bermata di tengkuk, atau berkaki empat, dan ciri utamanya memakan manusia.
claims.quote: The Romanian word appears to have meant "Dog-head" (căp being a form of cap, meaning "head", and căun a derivative of câine, "dog"). According to Romanian folkloric phantasy, the căpcăun has a dog head, sometimes with four eyes, with eyes in the nape, or with four legs, but whose main characteristic is anthropophagy.

claims.statement: In Romanian translations of other European works, creatures such as ogres or trolls are usually rendered as căpcăun.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Rumania karya Eropa lain, nama makhluk seperti ogre atau troll biasanya diterjemahkan sebagai căpcăun.
claims.quote: In most Romanian publications of other European works the names of creatures such as Ogres or Trolls are usually translated as căpcăun.

claims.statement: The term căpcăun also means 'Tatar chieftain' or 'Turkish chieftain', and 'pagan'.
claims.statement_id: Istilah căpcăun juga berarti "kepala suku Tatar" atau "kepala suku Turk", serta "kafir".
claims.quote: The term căpcăun also means "Tatar chieftain" or "Turk chieftain", as well "pagan".

claims.statement: Some linguists see căpcăun as an echo of the title kapkan (also kavhan, kaphan, kapgan) used by Central Asian peoples such as the Pannonian Avars, Bulgars and Pechenegs who invaded Eastern Europe.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian ahli bahasa menganggap căpcăun gema gelar kapkan (juga kavhan, kaphan, kapgan) yang dipakai suku-suku Asia Tengah seperti Avar Pannonia, Bulgar, dan Pecheneg yang menyerbu Eropa Timur.
claims.quote: Some linguists consider căpcăun to be an echo of a title or administrative rank, such as kapkan (also kavhan, kaphan, kapgan) used by various Central Asian tribes who invaded Eastern Europe during late antiquity and the medieval era, such as the Pannonian Avars, Bulgars and Pechenegs.

claims.statement: According to the Russian article, they are man-eaters that swallow children whole with one mouth and spit out the inedible remains from the other, and catch boys to fatten for slaughter.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, mereka pemakan manusia yang menelan anak bulat-bulat dengan satu mulut dan memuntahkan sisa yang tak termakan dari mulut lain, serta menangkap anak laki-laki untuk digemukkan sebelum disembelih.
claims.quote: Это людоеды, заглатывающие одним из своих ртов детей целиком или большие куски человеческого мяса прямо с костями и всем остальным, а из другого — выплёвывающие несъедобные отходы. Рассказывали, что они ловили мальчиков и откармливали их на убой.

claims.statement: The belief may come from the Greek romance Alexandria, translated into Romanian in 1620.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan ini mungkin berasal dari roman Yunani Alexandria, yang diterjemahkan ke bahasa Rumania pada 1620.
claims.quote: Поверье об этих существах возможно происходит из греческого романа «Александрия», который был переведён на румынский язык в 1620 году

claims.statement: In modern Romania căpcăun is used for a wicked, cruel, heartless person.
claims.statement_id: Di Rumania modern, căpcăun dipakai untuk menyebut orang yang jahat, kejam, dan tak berperasaan.
claims.quote: В современной Румынии кэпкэуном называют злого, жестокого и бессердечного человека.

claims.statement: The Catalan article also calls the căpcăun a creature of Romanian folklore shown as an ogre who kidnaps children or young ladies, mostly princesses.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Katalan juga menyebut căpcăun makhluk cerita rakyat Rumania berupa raksasa pemakan manusia yang menculik anak atau gadis, terutama putri raja.
claims.quote: Un căpcăun és una criatura del folklore romanès representada com un ogre que segresta nens o senyoretes (principalment princeses).

claims.statement: Cola Pesce or Pesce Cola ('Nicholas Fish') is an Italian folktale of a merman mentioned in literature from the 12th century, with many variants.
claims.statement_id: Cola Pesce atau Pesce Cola ("Nikolas Ikan") adalah dongeng Italia tentang manusia ikan yang disebut dalam sastra sejak abad ke-12, dengan banyak varian.
claims.quote: Cola Pesce, also known as Pesce Cola (i.e., "Nicholas Fish") is an Italian folktale about a merman, mentioned in literature as early as the 12th century. Many variants and retellings have been recorded.

claims.statement: The first literary mention is by the 12th-century Provençal poet Raimon Jordan, of a 'Nichola de Bar' (Nicholas of Bari) who lived among the fishes.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan sastra pertama berasal dari penyair abad ke-12 Raimon Jordan dari Provence tentang "Nichola de Bar" (Nikolas dari Bari) yang hidup bersama ikan.
claims.quote: The first known literary mention was by a 12th-century poet, Raimon Jordon of Provencal, who was referred to a "Nichola de Bar" (Nicholas of Bari) who lived with the fishes.

claims.statement: Walter Map recorded the story of Nicholas Pipe, who looked like a normal man but could live under the sea for long periods and warned ships of storms.
claims.statement_id: Walter Map mencatat kisah Nicholas Pipe yang tampak seperti manusia biasa tetapi dapat lama hidup di bawah laut dan memperingatkan kapal tentang badai.
claims.quote: Walter Map recorded a story of "Nicholas Pipe," who appeared like a normal human but had the ability to live under the sea for long periods of time, and would warn ships of storms.

claims.statement: In a Palermo version edited by Italo Calvino, Cola swims all the time until his exasperated mother curses him into a fish, and he at once becomes half fish, with duck feet and a frog's throat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Palermo yang disunting Italo Calvino, Cola terus berenang sampai ibunya yang kesal mengutuknya menjadi ikan, dan seketika ia menjadi setengah ikan berkaki bebek dan bertenggorokan katak.
claims.quote: In a version from Palermo, edited by Italo Calvino, Nick Fish spends all of his time swimming, until his frustrated mother curses him to turn into a fish. He instantly becomes half fish, with duck feet and a frog's throat.

claims.statement: He finds that Messina rests on three columns, some of them broken.
claims.statement_id: Ia mendapati Messina bertumpu pada tiga tiang, sebagian di antaranya patah.
claims.quote: Nick Fish discovers that Messina rests on three columns, some of which are broken

claims.statement: According to the German article, Colapesce, really Nikolaus or Cola, was a fisherman's son from Messina.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, Colapesce, sebenarnya Nikolaus atau Cola, adalah putra nelayan dari Messina.
claims.quote: Colapesce oder auch Cola Pesce, eigentlich Nikolaus, kurz Cola genannt, war Sohn eines Fischers aus Messina.

claims.statement: Emperor Frederick II, wanting to test him, threw a cup into the sea, and Colapesce brought it straight back up.
claims.statement_id: Kaisar Friedrich II ingin mengujinya, lalu melempar cangkir ke laut dan Colapesce segera mengambilnya kembali.
claims.quote: Der Kaiser ging daher mit einigen Beratern in einem Boot aufs Meer und warf eine Tasse ins Wasser, die sofort von Colapesce wieder heraufgeholt wurde.

claims.statement: The third time Frederick threw a ring into deeper water, and Colapesce never came back to the surface.
claims.statement_id: Pada kali ketiga Friedrich melempar cincin ke air yang lebih dalam, dan Colapesce tidak muncul lagi ke permukaan.
claims.quote: Beim dritten Mal soll Friedrich einen Ring in noch tieferes Wasser geworfen haben, doch Colaspesce erschien nicht mehr zurück an der Oberfläche.

claims.statement: On his last dive he saw Sicily stands on three columns, one of them rusted, and decided to stay under water holding it up so the island would not sink, and he holds it still.
claims.statement_id: Pada penyelaman terakhirnya ia melihat Sisilia berdiri di atas tiga tiang, satu di antaranya berkarat, dan ia memutuskan tinggal di bawah air menopang tiang itu agar pulau itu tidak tenggelam, dan ia masih menopangnya sampai kini.
claims.quote: so sah Colapesce bei seinem letzten Tauchgang für Friedrich, dass Sizilien auf drei Säulen gebaut ist, von denen eine verrostet war, und er beschloss, unter Wasser zu bleiben und für den Kaiser die Säule zu unterstützen, damit die Insel nicht unterginge und er stütze sie noch heute.

claims.statement: When the island shakes, it is said, he is tired and switching shoulders.
claims.statement_id: Konon bila pulau itu berguncang, ia sedang lelah dan memindahkan tiang ke bahu lainnya.
claims.quote: Wenn die Insel bebt, so heißt es, sei er erschöpft und wechsle die Schulter.

claims.statement: The Italian article calls Colapesce, Peix Nicolau in Catalan, an imaginary figure of European folklore whose legend has been passed down orally in many variants since the 12th century.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Italia menyebut Colapesce, dalam bahasa Katalan Peix Nicolau, tokoh khayalan cerita rakyat Eropa yang legendanya diwariskan lisan dalam banyak varian sejak abad ke-12.
claims.quote: Cola pesce, o Colapesce, in catalano Peix Nicolau, è un personaggio immaginario del folclore europeo, la cui leggenda è stata tramandata oralmente in molte varianti e le cui origini risalgono al XII secolo.

claims.statement: Iratxoak (singular iratxo) are the imps of Basque mythology, also called irelsuzko, irelu, ireltxu or iretxo.
claims.statement_id: Iratxoak (tunggal: iratxo) adalah peri usil mitologi Basque, juga disebut irelsuzko, irelu, ireltxu, atau iretxo.
claims.quote: Iratxoak (sing.: iratxo) are the imps of Basque mythology. Other names for them include irelsuzko/irelzuzko, irelu, irelixu/ireltxu, and iretxo.

claims.statement: They are generally seen as the Basque goblins or fairies, though a 1926 French-Basque dictionary renders iratxo as 'spectre'; treated well they help with house and farm work, but if offended they cause small troubles and play tricks.
claims.statement_id: Mereka umumnya dianggap padanan Basque untuk goblin atau peri, meski kamus Prancis-Basque tahun 1926 menerjemahkan iratxo sebagai hantu; bila diperlakukan baik mereka membantu pekerjaan rumah dan ladang, tetapi bila tersinggung mereka membuat masalah kecil dan mengerjai orang.
claims.quote: They are generally considered the Basque equivalent of goblins or fairies, although a French-Basque dictionary from 1926 translates the word iratxo as spectre (ghost). They are said to assist in household and farming tasks if treated well. If offended, iratxoak may cause the offender minor troubles or target them with tricks.

claims.statement: They are found in many places such as forests, caves and ruins, are tied to hidden treasure in some legends, and are nocturnal.
claims.statement_id: Mereka ada di banyak tempat seperti hutan, gua, dan reruntuhan, dalam sebagian legenda dikaitkan dengan harta tersembunyi, dan dianggap makhluk malam.
claims.quote: They are said to be found in many places, including forests, caves, and ruins. In some legends, iratxoak are associated with hidden treasure. Iratxoak are considered to be nocturnal.

claims.statement: At Saint John's Eve festivities, people dressed as iratxoak collect wishes and unwanted thoughts from the crowd and throw them into a bonfire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam perayaan malam Santo Yohanes, orang yang berkostum iratxo mengumpulkan harapan dan pikiran buruk para pengunjung lalu melemparkannya ke api unggun.
claims.quote: During Saint John's Eve festivities, people dressed as iratxoak may collect wishes and unwanted thoughts from attendees and toss them into a bonfire.

claims.statement: Galtxagorriak are a house-spirit kind of iratxo, more helpful to humans; their name means 'red pants'.
claims.statement_id: Galtxagorriak adalah jenis iratxo roh rumah yang lebih suka membantu manusia; namanya berarti "celana merah".
claims.quote: Galtxagorriak are a house spirit variety of iratxo that are more helpful to humans. Their name translates to "red-pants".

claims.statement: Some scholars think iratxo may be related to irasco, 'castrated goat'.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian sarjana menduga kata iratxo berkaitan dengan irasco, "kambing kebiri".
claims.quote: Some scholars believe that the word iratxo may be related to the word irasco, meaning "castrated goat".

claims.statement: According to the French article, Iratxo, Gorritxiki and Aiharra-Haio are malicious sprites, companions of the devil (deabru), sometimes described as imps.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Iratxo, Gorritxiki, dan Aiharra-Haio adalah peri usil jahat pengiring iblis (deabru) yang kadang digambarkan sebagai iblis kecil.
claims.quote: Iratxo, Gorritxiki, Aiharra-Haio sont des lutins maléfiques dans la mythologie basque. Ce sont des accompagnateurs du diable (deabru) et sont parfois décrits comme des diablotins.

claims.statement: Its name is directly linked to the fern (iratze in Basque).
claims.statement_id: Namanya dikaitkan langsung dengan tumbuhan pakis (iratze dalam bahasa Basque).
claims.quote: Son nom est cependant directement associé à la fougère (iratze en basque).

claims.statement: A proverb printed in 1596, 'Gassoto yrabacia / yrachoen da yracia', says that ill-gotten gains are taken away by Iratxo.
claims.statement_id: Pepatah dalam kumpulan tahun 1596, "Gassoto yrabacia / yrachoen da yracia", berarti keuntungan yang diperoleh secara curang akan diambil Iratxo.
claims.quote: Un proverbe publié au XVIe siècle (Énonciations et Sentences de 1596) se lit comme suit : Gassoto yrabacia / yrachoen da yracia. Ce dicton nous dit que les bénéfices obtenus de manière abusive, Iratxo vous les enlève.

claims.statement: The Spanish article calls the iratxo a kind of sprite of Basque mythology from old Biscayan legends.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Spanyol menyebut iratxo sejenis peri rumah mitologi Basque dari legenda lama Biscaya.
claims.quote: Iratxo (en plural en euskera: Iratxoak) es un tipo de duende de la mitología vasca de antiguas leyendas vizcaínas.

claims.statement: In Italian folklore Lariosauro is a lake monster said to live in Lake Como, about 50 km (30 miles) north of Milan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Italia, Lariosauro adalah monster danau yang konon tinggal di Danau Como, sekitar 50 km di utara Milan.
claims.quote: In Italian folklore, Lariosauro is a lake monster said to live in Lake Como in Italy, about 50 km (30 miles) north of Milan.

claims.statement: A sighting by two hunters on 18 November 1946 at Pian di Spagna was reported in the Corriere comasco, but it was entirely a press hoax.
claims.statement_id: Penampakan oleh dua pemburu pada 18 November 1946 di Pian di Spagna dilaporkan surat kabar Corriere comasco, tetapi sepenuhnya rekaan pers.
claims.quote: A sighting by two hunters was reported that on 18 November 1946 at Pian di Spagna (a reserve separated from Lake Como), was reported in the local newspaper Corriere comasco, but it was completely a hoax perpetrated by the press.

claims.statement: Achille Combi, who wrote the piece, said the monster's crested head rose from the water, its body was 2–3 metres long and 'bristling with extremely hard, reddish-brown scales'.
claims.statement_id: Achille Combi, penulis berita itu, menyebut kepala monster yang berjambul muncul dari air, panjang tubuhnya 2–3 meter, dan dipenuhi sisik keras berwarna cokelat kemerahan.
claims.quote: Achille Combi (who wrote the piece in  Corriere comasco) wrote that the crested head of the monster emerged out of water, its body length was 2–3 meters, and "bristling with extremely hard, reddish-brown scales".

claims.statement: A few days later La Provincia suggested it might have been a sturgeon.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa hari kemudian La Provincia menulis bahwa itu mungkin ikan sturgeon.
claims.quote: La Provincia published a follow-up piece a few days later suggesting it might have been a sturgeon.

claims.statement: The creature was nicknamed lariosauro, the name used a century earlier for a prehistoric reptile whose fossils were found by the lake (Lariosaurus balsami).
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu dijuluki lariosauro, nama yang seabad sebelumnya dipakai untuk reptil prasejarah yang fosilnya ditemukan di tepi danau (Lariosaurus balsami).
claims.quote: The creature earned the nickname lariosauro, but this was the same name legitimately used a century before to name a prehistoric reptile whose fossilized remains were found by the lake (Lariosaurus balsami).

claims.statement: The sceptical researcher Giorgio Castiglioni judged the 1954 animal an otter, the August 1957 monster a hoax, the September 1957 beast possibly a pike and the 2003 eel a group of fish swimming together.
claims.statement_id: Peneliti skeptis Giorgio Castiglioni menilai penampakan 1954 adalah berang-berang, monster Agustus 1957 rekaan, binatang September 1957 mungkin ikan pike, dan belut 2003 sekelompok ikan yang berenang bersama.
claims.quote: Skeptic researcher Giorgio Castiglioni, who studied these cases, thinks that the animal of 1954 was an otter, the monster of August 1957 a hoax, the beast of September 1957 possibly a pike, and the 2003 eel was a group of fish swimming together.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, in 2003 a giant eel some 10–12 m long was sighted at Lecco.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, pada 2003 terlihat belut raksasa sepanjang 10–12 m di Lecco.
claims.quote: En 2003 se avistó una anguila gigante de unos 10 – 12 m, en Lecco.

claims.statement: The Lithuanian article says that in 1946 witnesses reported seeing a reptile-like animal swimming in the lake.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Lituania menyebut pada 1946 saksi melaporkan melihat hewan mirip reptil berenang di danau.
claims.quote: 1946 m. liudininkai pranešė, kad matė į roplį panašų gyvūną, plaukusį ežere.

claims.statement: The Spanish legend of la Encantada is a generic name for a set of oral traditions and mythological legends told in many Spanish localities.
claims.statement_id: Legenda Spanyol la Encantada adalah nama umum untuk sekumpulan tradisi lisan dan legenda mitologis yang diceritakan di banyak tempat di Spanyol.
claims.quote: The Spanish legend of la Encantada is a generic name that refers to a set of oral traditions and legends mythological narrated in numerous Spanish localities.

claims.statement: Despite many local variants, common elements are a young long-haired woman, St John's Eve, her appearing while combing her hair, and a mirror, a wedding and a comb, usually golden.
claims.statement_id: Meski banyak varian, unsurnya sama: tokoh utama perempuan muda berambut panjang, waktu malam Santo Yohanes, penampakan sambil menyisir rambut, serta cermin, pernikahan, dan sisir yang biasanya emas.
claims.quote: Although there are multiple local variants, a series of elements are common: the protagonist (a young woman with long hair), the time (St. John's Eve), the manifestation (combing her hair) and other elements (mirror, wedding, comb—generally gold).

claims.statement: La Encantada is said to be closely related to the Lamias, the Mouras (Galicia), Mari and Mairu (Basque), the Anjanas (Cantabria) and the Xanas (Asturias).
claims.statement_id: La Encantada konon berkerabat dekat dengan Lamia, Moura (Galisia), Mari dan Mairu (Basque), Anjana (Cantabria), dan Xana (Asturias).
claims.quote: La Encantada is supposedly closely related to mythological beings such as the Lamias, Mouras (Galician mythology), Mari and Mairu (Basque mythology), the Anjanas (Cantabrian mythology) and the Xanas (Asturian mythology)

claims.statement: Its link with the Mexican figure Xtabay suggests a very ancient, almost universal myth.
claims.statement_id: Hubungannya dengan tokoh Meksiko Xtabay menunjukkan mitos ini sangat tua dan hampir universal.
claims.quote: Likewise, its relationship with the Mexican figure Xtabay suggests a very ancient and almost universal presence of the myth

claims.statement: The term encantada, 'enchanted', is common in Spanish place names and usually marks the apparition.
claims.statement_id: Istilah encantada, "yang tersihir", cukup umum dalam nama tempat di Spanyol dan biasanya menandai tempat penampakan.
claims.quote: The term encantada ("enchanted") is quite common in Spanish toponymy and microtoponymy and, normally, designates the apparition.

claims.statement: Gálmez de Fuentes sees the place name as a later adaptation of the pre-Roman *kanto, 'stone, stony shore'.
claims.statement_id: Gálmez de Fuentes menganggap nama tempat itu adaptasi belakangan dari istilah pra-Romawi *kanto, "batu, pantai berbatu".
claims.quote: Gálmez de Fuentes considers said toponym as an explanation or a posteriori adaptation of the Pre-Roman term *kanto ("stone, stony shore").

claims.statement: The place name often appears as mora encantada, suggesting sites from the Muslim period, though many are older.
claims.statement_id: Nama tempat sering berbentuk mora encantada, yang bisa membuat orang mengira situs itu dari masa kekuasaan Muslim, padahal banyak yang lebih tua.
claims.quote: Many times the toponym is presented under the form mora encantada ("enchanted mora"), which may lead to believe that the sites are from the period of the Muslim domination. This is not true, since many of them are earlier

claims.statement: At Las Camarillas (Hellín), in the early morning of St John's Day (24 June), a very white lady with very long blonde hair used to appear at the foot of the Camareta cave.
claims.statement_id: Di Las Camarillas (Hellín), pada dini hari Santo Yohanes (24 Juni) seorang perempuan sangat putih berambut pirang sangat panjang biasa muncul di kaki gua Camareta.
claims.quote: In the early morning of St. John's Day (June 24), a very white lady with very long blonde hair used to appear at the foot of the Camareta cave

claims.statement: She asked passers-by whether they liked the comb or her more; when a shepherd chose the comb she cried, 'Damn you, because of you I will stay enchanted!'
claims.statement_id: Ia bertanya kepada yang lewat mana yang lebih disukai, sisir atau dirinya; ketika seorang gembala memilih sisir, ia berseru, "Terkutuklah kau, karenamu aku tetap tersihir!"
claims.quote: They say that on a certain occasion a shepherd passed by and when she asked him the question, he answered that it was the comb, and she exclaimed: "Damn you, because of you I will continue to be enchanted!"

claims.statement: At Rojales, la Encantá asks a brave man to carry her to the Segura River to bathe her feet and so break the curse.
claims.statement_id: Di Rojales, la Encantá meminta pemberani menggendongnya ke Sungai Segura untuk membasuh kakinya agar kutukannya patah.
claims.quote: If a brave man meets her, la Encantá will ask him to carry her in his arms to the Segura River to bathe her feet and thus break the curse.

claims.statement: The Spanish article likewise calls la Encantada a generic name for oral traditions and legends in many Spanish places.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Spanyol juga menyebut la Encantada nama umum untuk tradisi lisan dan legenda di banyak tempat di Spanyol.
claims.quote: La Leyenda española de la Encantada es un nombre genérico que hace referencia a un conjunto de tradiciones orales y leyendas mitológicas narradas en numerosas localidades españolas.

claims.statement: The Portuguese article says the same.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Portugis menyebut hal yang sama.
claims.quote: A Lenda espanhola da Encantada é um nome genérico que faz referência a um conjunto de tradições orais e lendas mitológicas narradas em numerosas localidades espanholas.

claims.statement: Lou Carcolh is a mythical beast of French folklore, a large, slimy, snail-like serpent with hairy tentacles and a big shell, said to live in a cave beneath Hastingues in the Landes, south-west France.
claims.statement_id: Lou Carcolh adalah binatang mitis cerita rakyat Prancis berupa ular mirip siput yang besar dan berlendir, bertentakel berbulu dan bercangkang besar, yang konon tinggal di gua di bawah Hastingues, Landes, Prancis barat daya.
claims.quote: Lou Carcolh, or the Carcolh, is a mythical beast from French folklore. It is described as a large, slimy, snail-like serpent with hairy tentacles and a large shell. It is said to live in a cavern beneath Hastingues, a town in the Les Landes region in southwestern France.

claims.statement: Its slime could sometimes be seen long before it arrived, and its long-reaching tentacles grabbed prey and dragged it into its cave without its leaving.
claims.statement_id: Lendirnya kadang terlihat jauh sebelum makhluk itu tiba, dan tentakelnya yang sangat panjang dipakai untuk meraih dan menyeret mangsa ke guanya tanpa ia keluar.
claims.quote: It is described to have a slime that could sometimes be seen long before the creature itself arrived, and its tentacles had a great reach that would be used to grab and drag prey into its cave without leaving.

claims.statement: According to the French article the carcolh is a monstrous snail of Landes folklore peculiar to Hastingues, but references to it are no older than the early 20th century.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, carcolh adalah siput raksasa dari cerita rakyat Landes khas kota Hastingues, tetapi rujukan tentangnya tidak lebih tua dari awal abad ke-20.
claims.quote: Le carcolh (lou carcolh en gascon) est un escargot monstrueux appartenant au folklore du département français des Landes et propre à la ville de Hastingues. Toutefois, les références à cette créature ne sont pas antérieures au début du XXe siècle.

claims.statement: By legend the hill that sheltered the town also held a cave housing a carcolh, a fearsome monstrous snail that frightened the inhabitants away and emptied the town.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, bukit yang melindungi kota itu juga menyimpan gua tempat tinggal carcolh, siput mengerikan yang membuat penduduk ketakutan, pergi, dan kota pun sepi.
claims.quote: Mais, selon la légende, le tuc, qui offre protection, renferme également une caverne qui abrite un Carcolh, escargot formidable et monstrueux, qui serait la cause du départ des habitants, poussés par la peur, et du dépeuplement de la cité.

claims.statement: The legend is encouraged by the hill's rounded shape, like a snail's shell.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini didukung bentuk bukit yang bulat seperti cangkang siput.
claims.quote: Cette légende est favorisée par la forme arrondie du promontoire, rappelant celle d'une coquille d'escargot.

claims.statement: The Revue de Gascogne of 1903 mentions a monstrous snail living in a vast, dark cave over which, by tradition, the town of Hastingues is built.
claims.statement_id: Revue de Gascogne tahun 1903 menyebut siput raksasa yang tinggal di gua besar dan gelap yang di atasnya, menurut tradisi, berdiri kota Hastingues.
claims.quote: Concernant le Carcolh, la Revue de Gascogne de 1903 évoque un ... Escargot monstrueux qui a son gîte dans une vaste et sombre caverne au-dessus de laquelle est bâtie, d'après les traditions, la ville de Hastingues.

claims.statement: The Russian article says sunlight frightens the snail, so it never comes to the surface.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Rusia menyebut cahaya matahari menakutkan siput ini sehingga ia tidak muncul ke permukaan.
claims.quote: Также считается, что солнечный свет пугает улитку, поэтому она не показывается на поверхности.

claims.statement: The Luisón (Paraguayan Guarani Luisõ; Spanish Luisón or Lobizón) is one of the seven legendary beasts of Paraguay, the seventh and last son of Tau and Kerana; the myth is also known in Argentina and holds that in a family of seven sons the last will become a Luisón.
claims.statement_id: Luisón (Guarani Paraguay: Luisõ; Spanyol: Luisón atau Lobizón) adalah satu dari tujuh binatang legendaris Paraguay, putra ketujuh dan terakhir Tau dan Kerana; mitos ini juga dikenal di Argentina dan menyebut bahwa dalam keluarga dengan tujuh anak laki-laki, anak terakhir akan menjadi Luisón.
claims.quote: The Luison (Paraguayan Guaraní: Luisõ; Spanish: Luisón or Lobizón) is one of the seven legendary beasts of Paraguay, and is the seventh and last son of Tau and Kerana. The myth is known also in Argentina and says that in a family with seven male children, the last child will become Luisón.

claims.statement: In the original myth, as the seventh child of Tau and Kerana he was the most accursed, looking like a giant, hideous dog.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi asli, sebagai anak ketujuh Tau dan Kerana ia paling terkutuk, tampak seperti anjing raksasa yang sangat buruk rupa.
claims.quote: In the original version of the myth, Luisón was the seventh and last child of Tau and Kerana, and thus was the most accursed. He appeared to be a giant dog, and was said to be extremely ugly, even horrendous looking.

claims.statement: The myth says a family's seventh son will transform on his 13th birthday.
claims.statement_id: Mitos menyebut anak laki-laki ketujuh dalam keluarga akan berubah pada ulang tahunnya yang ke-13.
claims.quote: The myth tells that the seventh son in a family will transform on his 13th birthday.

claims.statement: The maned wolf, a slender long-legged wolf-like canid with a shambling gait, fitted the werewolf image brought by settlers and was eventually blended with local Guarani myths.
claims.statement_id: Serigala surai, anjing liar ramping berkaki panjang yang berjalan terseok, cocok dengan gambaran manusia serigala yang dibawa pendatang dan akhirnya berpadu dengan mitos Guarani setempat.
claims.quote: The maned wolf, a slender, wolf-like, stilted canid that moves with shambling steps, fitted the popular depiction of the werewolf and ultimately it was syncretized with local guarani myths.

claims.statement: Since the 19th century the President of Argentina has customarily been godparent to every seventh son, a custom born because superstitious people sometimes sacrificed their seventh son for fear he was a Luisón.
claims.statement_id: Sejak abad ke-19 Presiden Argentina biasa menjadi wali baptis setiap anak laki-laki ketujuh, kebiasaan yang muncul karena orang yang percaya takhayul kadang mengorbankan anak ketujuh mereka karena takut ia Luisón.
claims.quote: It has been customary since the 19th century for the President of Argentina to be named the "godparent" of each seventh male child of a married couple. This custom arose because superstitious people sometimes sacrificed their seventh son out of fear of the "possibility" that a Luisón had been born.

claims.statement: On 12 March 1973 President Juan Domingo Perón made the custom law through Decree No. 848, the presidential sponsorship law.
claims.statement_id: Pada 12 Maret 1973 Presiden Juan Domingo Perón meresmikan kebiasaan ini lewat Dekret No. 848, yang dikenal sebagai undang-undang perwalian presiden.
claims.quote: On 12 March 1973, President Juan Domingo Perón gave legal form to this custom through Decree No. 848, known as the presidential sponsorship law.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, as the seventh son of Tau and Keraná he bears his parents' heaviest curse; his very name terrifies, and he stands at the crossroads of life and death.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, sebagai putra ketujuh Tau dan Keraná ia menanggung kutukan terberat orang tuanya; namanya saja menakutkan, dan ia berada di persimpangan jalan kehidupan dan kematian.
claims.quote: Luisón es el séptimo hijo de Tau y Keraná en la mitología guaraní, sobre él cayó la mayor maldición que pesaba sobre los progenitores. Su solo nombre aterroriza. Este ser espeluznante se encuentra ubicado en la encrucijada de los caminos de la vida y de la muerte.

claims.statement: According to the Portuguese article it is believed to look like a South American wolf or a red-eyed monkey, with fish fins and a huge tapir-like phallus.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Portugis, ia dipercaya mirip serigala Amerika Selatan atau monyet bermata merah, bersirip ikan, dan berzakar besar seperti tapir.
claims.quote: Acredita-se que seja semelhante a um lobo sul-americano ou a um macaco de olhos vermelhos, com barbatanas de peixe e um enorme falo (de anta).

claims.statement: On full-moon nights falling on Friday and/or Tuesday the person turned into a half-animal creature.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam bulan purnama hari Jumat atau Selasa, orang itu berubah menjadi makhluk setengah binatang.
claims.quote: nas noites de lua cheia de sexta-feira e/ou terça-feira, o indivíduo se transformava em uma criatura com metade das característica

claims.statement: A matagot is a spirit of French folklore that usually takes the form of a black cat.
claims.statement_id: Matagot adalah roh dalam cerita rakyat Prancis yang biasanya berwujud kucing hitam.
claims.quote: A Matagot is a spirit in French folklore that tends to take the form of a black cat.

claims.statement: Matagots are generally evil, but some help, like the 'magician cat' that brings wealth to a home if well fed.
claims.statement_id: Matagot umumnya jahat, tetapi sebagian dapat membantu, seperti "kucing penyihir" yang membawa kekayaan ke rumah bila diberi makan dengan baik.
claims.quote: Matagots are generally evil, but some may prove helpful, like the "magician cat" said to bring wealth into a home if it is well fed.

claims.statement: A wealth-bringing matagot must be lured with a fresh plump chicken and carried home without its new owner looking back.
claims.statement_id: Matagot pembawa kekayaan harus dipancing dengan ayam segar yang gemuk, lalu dibawa pulang tanpa pemiliknya menoleh ke belakang.
claims.quote: Traditionally, a wealth-bringing matagot must be lured with a fresh, plump chicken, then carried home by its new owner without the human looking back.

claims.statement: If the cat gets the first mouthful of food and drink at every meal and is well treated, it brings good luck; a matagot can serve up to nine masters at once.
claims.statement_id: Bila kucing itu diberi suapan pertama makanan dan minuman setiap kali makan dan dirawat baik, ia membawa keberuntungan; matagot konon dapat melayani sampai sembilan tuan sekaligus.
claims.quote: If the cat is given the first mouthful of food and drink at every meal and otherwise treated well, it will bring the human good fortune. A matagot is said to be able to serve up to nine masters at once.

claims.statement: In Gascon tradition one must not keep the matagot for life: a dying owner suffers a long agony until he frees it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi Gascogne, matagot tidak boleh dipelihara seumur hidup: pemilik yang sekarat akan lama menderita selama belum membebaskannya.
claims.quote: In Gascony traditions, you must not keep the matagot all your life: if the owner is dying, they will suffer a long agony, as long as they don't free the matagot.

claims.statement: In Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald the matagot is a hairless black cat-like creature that can multiply at will.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald, matagot adalah makhluk mirip kucing hitam tak berbulu yang dapat menggandakan diri.
claims.quote: In Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald the matagot is a hairless, black, cat-like creature with the ability to multiply at will.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the chat d'argent, mandragot or matagot of Breton, Gascon, Provençal and Languedoc folklore is a usually black, diabolical cat a sorcerer obtains in exchange for his soul.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, chat d'argent, mandragot, atau matagot dalam cerita rakyat Bretagne, Gascogne, Provence, dan Languedoc adalah kucing setan, biasanya hitam, yang diperoleh penyihir dengan menukar jiwanya.
claims.quote: Le chat d'argent, mandragot ou matagot est, dans le folklore de Bretagne, de Gascogne, de Provence, et du Languedoc, un chat généralement noir et diabolique obtenu par un sorcier en échange de son âme.

claims.statement: It roams mysterious places at night and returns at dawn with gold louis for its master; if neglected or unrewarded it takes offence and may take cruel revenge.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkeliaran di tempat misterius pada malam hari dan pulang saat fajar membawa koin emas louis untuk tuannya; bila diabaikan atau tidak diberi imbalan, ia tersinggung dan dapat membalas dengan kejam.
