claims.quote: Il est censé se promener dans quelques lieux mystérieux pendant la nuit, et revenir à l'aube avec un stock de louis d'or pour son maître. Si celui-ci le néglige ou ne le récompense pas, le chat s'offense et peut se venger cruellement.

claims.statement: Sometimes the cat serves nine masters and leads the last to hell.
claims.statement_id: Kadang kucing ini melayani sembilan tuan dan membawa tuan terakhir ke neraka.
claims.quote: Parfois, ce chat serait censé servir non pas un, mais neuf maîtres, et conduire le dernier en enfer.

claims.statement: The Catalan article calls the matagot, also mantagot, a spirit of Occitan mythology known especially in Provence and Languedoc.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Katalan menyebut matagot, juga mantagot, roh mitologi Occitania yang terutama dikenal di Provence dan Languedoc.
claims.quote: El matagot (en occità: lo matagòt), anomenat també mantagot (mantagòt), és un geni propi de la mitologia d'Occitània, conegut sobretot a la Provença i el Llenguadoc.

claims.statement: A minairó (plural minairons), also manairó, menairó, diablorí in Catalonia or zaingorriak in the Basque Country, is a tiny mythical being that some people keep shut in a needle case in villages of the Pyrenees.
claims.statement_id: Minairó (jamak minairons), juga manairó, menairó, diablorí di Katalonia atau zaingorriak di negeri Basque, adalah makhluk mitis mungil yang di beberapa desa Pyrenees disimpan dalam tabung jarum.
claims.quote: A minairó (Catalan pronunciation: [minəjˈɾo], plural minairons), also called manairó, menairó, diablorí in Catalonia or zaingorriak in the Basque country, is a tiny mythological being that some people save enclosed within a needle tube in some villages of the Pyrenees.

claims.statement: Minairons come from St John's-wort, which blooms on St John's Night (the summer solstice), grows in very deep caves guarded by giants and dragons, and can only be taken at midnight on St John's Day.
claims.statement_id: Minairons berasal dari tumbuhan St John's-wort yang mekar pada malam Santo Yohanes (titik balik matahari musim panas), tumbuh di gua sangat dalam yang dijaga raksasa dan naga, dan hanya dapat diambil tepat tengah malam hari Santo Yohanes.
claims.quote: The minairons come from the perforate St John's-wort which blooms at the Saint John’s (the summer solstice) night. It grows in very deep caves guarded by giants and dragons and it only can be caught in the point of midnight on St. John’s Day.

claims.statement: Some say they are like a swarm of tiny, almost invisible mosquitoes; others compare them to bees for the buzzing they make leaving the needle case.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menyebut mereka seperti kawanan nyamuk kecil yang hampir tak terlihat, yang lain membandingkannya dengan lebah karena dengungnya saat keluar dari tabung jarum.
claims.quote: Others say that they are as a swarm of tiny mosquitoes, almost invisible. Some people prefer to compare them with the bee, because of the noise they do buzzing when left the needles’ tube or cane.

claims.statement: They are so tiny that thousands fit in the case, and when they come out they demand work, saying, 'What shall we do? What shall we say?'
claims.statement_id: Mereka begitu kecil sehingga ribuan muat dalam tabung, dan begitu keluar mereka menuntut pekerjaan sambil berkata, "Apa yang kita kerjakan? Apa yang kita katakan?"
claims.quote: No one doubts, however, that they are so tiny that inside the cane there must be thousands and when one foregrounds, eager demands for work, saying, "What will we do? What will we say?”

claims.statement: Legend says many of the Pyrenean screes are their work, made when a master opened the needle case by mistake.
claims.statement_id: Legenda menyebut banyak hamparan batu longsoran di Pyrenees adalah buatan mereka ketika tuannya tidak sengaja membuka tabung jarum.
claims.quote: The legend says that many of the screes of the Pyrenees have been works of these goblins, when his master opened the needle tube by mistake or accident

claims.statement: A few heirs of great Pyrenean houses reputedly owned the case, through which their house rose like a mushroom.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah pewaris rumah besar di Pyrenees konon memiliki tabung itu, sehingga rumah mereka makmur dengan cepat.
claims.quote: A handful of heirs of the Pyrenees main houses have been, on occasion, owners of the cane, through which the house went up like a mushroom.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, when the case was opened, if the opener did not set them work at once, the minairons killed him.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, bila tabung dibuka dan pembukanya tidak segera memberi pekerjaan, minairons membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Al abrirse el canuto, los minairones salían y decían: què farem?, què direm? -"¿qué haremos, qué diremos?"- y si la persona que lo había abierto no les ordenaba hacer algún trabajo inmediatamente, lo mataban

claims.statement: According to the French article, the Basque counterpart, mamarro or mamarroak, are small spirits who help with daily tasks and protect the family they live with.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, padanan Basque-nya, mamarro atau mamarroak, adalah roh kecil yang membantu pekerjaan sehari-hari dan melindungi keluarga tempat mereka tinggal.
claims.quote: Mamarro ou les mamarroak sont des Ireluak ou génies de petite taille issus de la mythologie basque, ils aident les gens dans leurs tâches quotidiennes et protègent la famille dans laquelle ils vivent.

claims.statement: These little elves are also called Galtzagorriak, Prakagorriak and Zaingorriak at Ordizia, among other names.
claims.statement_id: Peri kecil ini juga disebut Galtzagorriak, Prakagorriak, dan Zaingorriak di Ordizia, di antara nama lain.
claims.quote: Ces petits elfes portent les noms de Galtzagorriak, Prakagorriak, Famerijaleak à Kortezubi, Beharreztanak à Orozko, Aidetikakoak à Sare, Patuak ou Patuek à Ibarruri, Zaingorriak à Ordizia

claims.statement: In Basque mythology Odei, also Hodei, is a spirit of thunder and the personification of storm clouds.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Basque, Odei atau Hodei adalah roh guntur dan personifikasi awan badai.
claims.quote: In Basque mythology, Odei, also known as Hodei, is a spirit of thunder and the personification of storm clouds.

claims.statement: Odei, Hodei or Odai is a name sometimes given to thunder, to the great storm cloud, or to 'the one who thunders'.
claims.statement_id: Odei, Hodei, atau Odai adalah nama yang kadang dipakai untuk guntur, untuk awan badai besar, atau untuk "dia yang bergemuruh".
claims.quote: Odei, Hodei ou Odai est le nom dans la mythologie basque que l'on donne parfois pour désigner le tonnerre. D'autres appellent ainsi le gros nuage de tempête ou plus simplement l'agent du tonnerre, celui qui tonne.

claims.statement: On hearing thunder people say 'Odeiak jo', 'the thunderer has struck'.
claims.statement_id: Saat terdengar guntur orang berkata "Odeiak jo", "yang bergemuruh telah memukul".
claims.quote: Quand on entend tonner on dit : « Odeiak jo » (« celui qui tonne a frappé »).

claims.statement: At Gesalibar in Arrasate (Gipuzkoa) the south-east wind that brings storms is called Odeiaixe, 'Odei's wind'.
claims.statement_id: Di Gesalibar, Arrasate (Gipuzkoa), angin tenggara pembawa badai disebut Odeiaixe, "angin Odei".
claims.quote: Au quartier de Gesalibar, Arrasate (Guipuscoa) on appelle Odeiaixe « vent d'Odei » ou « vent du tonnerre », est un vent du sud-est qui apporte des tempêtes et des bourrasques.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article he frightened farmers by ruining their crops with lightning, appeared as a storm cloud, the spirit or god of the skies, successor to the old god Ortzi or Urtzi.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, ia menakuti petani dengan merusak panen lewat petirnya, tampak sebagai awan badai, roh atau dewa langit, pengganti dewa lama Ortzi atau Urtzi.
claims.quote: Atemorizaba a los campesinos echándoles a perder sus cosechas con sus rayos. Según los relatos, se muestra en forma de nube de tormenta, siendo el genio o dios de los cielos. Fue el sustituto del antiguo dios Ortzi o Urtzi.

claims.statement: In legends he sometimes appears as the wicked son of Mari, chief of the spirits.
claims.statement_id: Kadang dalam legenda ia muncul sebagai putra jahat Mari, pemimpin para roh.
claims.quote: Ocasionalmente, aparece en las leyendas como hijo malvado de Mari, jefa de los genios.

claims.statement: At Saint-Esteben (Labourd) people light blessed candles, burn laurel twigs or set an axe edge-up on the doorstep to ward him off and calm his fury.
claims.statement_id: Di Saint-Esteben (Lapurdi) orang menyalakan lilin yang diberkati, membakar ranting laurel, atau menaruh kapak dengan mata menghadap ke atas di ambang pintu untuk meredakan amarahnya.
claims.quote: En Saint-Esteben (Labort) se encienden velas bendecidas, se queman ramas de laurel en la casa o se sitúa un hacha en el umbral de la puerta principal de la casa, con el filo hacia arriba, para conjurarlo y aplacar su furia.

claims.statement: A pricolici (same form in the plural) is a Romanian vampire with werewolf traits, arising from a child breastfed again after weaning.
claims.statement_id: Pricolici (bentuk jamaknya sama) adalah vampir Rumania bercirikan manusia serigala, yang berasal dari anak yang disusui lagi setelah disapih.
claims.quote: A Pricolici (pronounced /pri.koˈlit͡ʃʲ/) (same form in plural) is a Romanian vampire with werewolf-like attributes, transformed from a child breastfed after its mother has weaned it risks.

claims.statement: Pricolici resemble the vârcolac, but always have wolf traits and can turn into ordinary people or animals.
claims.statement_id: Pricolici mirip vârcolac, tetapi selalu bercirikan serigala dan dapat berubah menjadi manusia biasa atau hewan.
claims.quote: Pricolici are similar to a vârcolac, although the latter sometimes symbolises a goblin, whereas the pricolici always has wolf-like characteristics, they have the ability to transform into ordinary people or animals.

claims.statement: Unlike the strigoi, which keeps a human look, the pricolici always resembles a wolf or dog; wicked, violent men are often said to become pricolici after death to keep harming people.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari strigoi yang tetap mirip manusia, pricolici selalu mirip serigala atau anjing; lelaki jahat dan kejam sering dikatakan menjadi pricolici setelah mati untuk terus mencelakai manusia.
claims.quote: While a strigoi possesses anthropomorphic qualities similar to the ones it had before death, a pricolici always resembles a wolf or dog. Malicious, violent men are often said to become pricolici after death, in order to continue harming other humans.

claims.statement: Some Romanian folklore holds that pricolici are werewolves in life and return as vampires after death.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian cerita rakyat Rumania menyebut pricolici adalah manusia serigala semasa hidup dan kembali sebagai vampir setelah mati.
claims.quote: Some Romanian folklore delineates that Pricolici are werewolves in life and after they die, return as vampires.

claims.statement: Even in modern times many rural Romanians have claimed to be attacked by unusually large, fierce wolves that strike silently, suddenly and only lone victims.
claims.statement_id: Bahkan di zaman modern banyak warga pedesaan Rumania mengaku diserang serigala yang luar biasa besar dan buas, yang menyerang diam-diam, tiba-tiba, dan hanya orang yang sendirian.
claims.quote: Even as recently as modern times, many people living in rural areas of Romania have claimed to have been viciously attacked by abnormally large and fierce wolves. Apparently, these wolves attack silently, unexpectedly and only solitary targets.

claims.statement: The word's origin is unknown, though it may come from Latin lycus, 'wolf'.
claims.statement_id: Asal katanya tidak diketahui, tetapi mungkin dari bahasa Latin lycus, "serigala".
claims.quote: The etymology of the word is unknown; although it probably has Latin origins from the word "Lycus" i.e "wolf" (prico+lici).

claims.statement: The Spanish article also calls them werewolves in life who return as vampires, the root of the legend of vampires turning into wolves, dogs, owls or bats.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Spanyol juga menyebut mereka manusia serigala semasa hidup yang kembali sebagai vampir, asal legenda vampir yang dapat menjadi serigala, anjing, burung hantu, atau kelelawar.
claims.quote: Algunos folclores rumano describen a los Pricolici como hombres lobo en vida que después de morir, regresan como vampiros. Esto también da lugar a la leyenda de los vampiros que pueden transformarse en animales como lobos, perros, búhos o murciélagos.

claims.statement: According to the Russian article, pricolici were the dead risen from the grave as wolves or dogs, and also living people able to turn into wolves or dogs for a time.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, pricolici adalah sebutan untuk orang mati yang bangkit dari kubur berwujud serigala atau anjing, maupun orang hidup yang untuk sementara dapat berubah menjadi serigala atau anjing.
claims.quote: Приколичами называли: мертвецов, вставших из могилы в образе волка или собаки, реже других диких животных; живых людей, способных на время превращаться в волков или собак

claims.statement: The Quinotaur (Latin Quinotaurus) is a mythical sea creature in the 7th-century Chronicle of Fredegar, 'the beast of Neptune which resembles a Quinotaur', held to have fathered Meroveus by attacking the wife of the Frankish king Chlodio and so sired the Merovingian kings.
claims.statement_id: Quinotaur (Latin: Quinotaurus) adalah makhluk laut mitis yang disebut dalam Kronik Fredegar abad ke-7 sebagai "binatang Neptunus yang menyerupai Quinotaur", yang dianggap menjadi ayah Meroveus dengan menyerang istri raja Frank Chlodio sehingga menurunkan raja-raja Merovingia.
claims.quote: The Quinotaur (Latin: Quinotaurus) is a mythical sea creature mentioned in the 7th century Frankish Chronicle of Fredegar. Referred to as "the beast of Neptune which resembles a Quinotaur", it was held to have fathered Meroveus by attacking the wife of the Frankish king Chlodio and thus to have sired the line of Merovingian kings.

claims.statement: The 'bull with five horns' was likened by Pseudo-Fredegar, interpolating Gregory of Tours, to both Neptune and the Minotaur, being both seaborne and bull-like.
claims.statement_id: "Banteng bertanduk lima" ini oleh Pseudo-Fredegar, yang menambahkan catatan Gregorius dari Tours, disamakan dengan Neptunus dan Minotaurus karena berasal dari laut dan berwujud banteng.
claims.quote: The "bull with five horns" was likened by Pseudo-Fredegar (interpolating Gregory of Tours, who authored an earlier record of the legend) to both Neptune and the Minotaur, as it was both seaborne and taurine.

claims.statement: It is unknown whether the sea and bull traits are original or added by the Christian authors, and the clerical Latin name does not show whether it translates a genuine Frankish creature or is a coinage.
claims.statement_id: Tidak diketahui apakah ciri laut dan banteng itu asli dari legenda atau tambahan penulis Kristen, dan nama Latinnya tidak menunjukkan apakah ia terjemahan makhluk Frank asli atau ciptaan baru.
claims.quote: It is not known whether one or both traits are original to the legend or if their combination is an accretion by one or both of the Christian authors. The clerical Latinity of the name does not indicate whether it is a translation of some genuine Frankish creature or a coining.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the name Quinotaurus means 'bull with five horns'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, nama Quinotaurus berarti "banteng bertanduk lima".
claims.quote: Le Quinotaure (Lat. Quinotaurus, « taureau à cinq cornes ») est une créature marine légendaire mentionnée dans la Chronique de Frédégaire du VIIe siècle.

claims.statement: It is considered the father of Merovech after raping Queen Altina, wife of the Frankish king Chlodio the Long-Haired.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap ayah Mérovée setelah memerkosa Ratu Altina, istri raja Frank Clodion si Berambut Panjang.
claims.quote: Il est considéré comme le père de Mérovée (et donc à l'origine de la lignée des rois mérovingiens) à la suite du viol de la reine Altina, épouse du roi franc Clodion le Chevelu.

claims.statement: The Italian article says it coupled with King Chlodio's wife while she was bathing in the sea.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Italia menyebut makhluk ini bersetubuh dengan istri raja Clodione ketika ia sedang mandi di laut.
claims.quote: Esso è ritenuto essere il padre di Meroveo, in quanto si unì alla moglie del re franco Clodione mentre ella stava facendo il bagno in mare

claims.statement: El Ratoncito Pérez or Ratón Pérez ('Pérez the Little Mouse') is a fantasy figure of early childhood in Spanish and Hispanic American cultures.
claims.statement_id: Ratoncito Pérez atau Ratón Pérez ("Tikus Kecil Pérez") adalah tokoh khayalan masa kanak-kanak dalam budaya Spanyol dan Amerika Hispanik.
claims.quote: El Ratoncito Pérez or Ratón Pérez ... Perez the Little Mouse or Perez Mouse) is a fantasy figure of early childhood in Spanish and Hispanic American cultures.

claims.statement: By tradition, children who lose a milk tooth put it under the pillow or on the bedside table, and he comes while they sleep and replaces it with a small payment or gift, like the Tooth Fairy elsewhere.
claims.statement_id: Menurut tradisi, anak yang tanggal gigi susunya menaruhnya di bawah bantal atau di meja samping tempat tidur, lalu Pérez datang saat mereka tidur dan menggantinya dengan uang atau hadiah kecil, seperti Peri Gigi di budaya lain.
claims.quote: The folklore states that when children lose one of their milk teeth, they should place it underneath their pillow or on their bedside table and he will visit while they sleep, replacing the lost tooth with a small payment or gift, as does the Tooth Fairy in other cultures.

claims.statement: He first appeared in oral folktales such as The Vain Little Mouse, but it was Luis Coloma who in 1894 made him a tooth collector in a tale written for the eight-year-old King Alfonso XIII.
claims.statement_id: Ia pertama muncul dalam dongeng lisan seperti El ratoncito vanidoso, tetapi Luis Coloma-lah yang pada 1894 menjadikannya pengumpul gigi dalam cerita untuk Raja Alfonso XIII yang berusia delapan tahun.
claims.quote: Although he first appeared in oral tradition folktales such as The Vain Little Mouse, it was Luis Coloma who in 1894 turned him into a tooth dealer in a tale written for an eight-year-old King Alfonso XIII.

claims.statement: Queen Maria Christina commissioned the tale for Alfonso XIII, who had just lost a tooth; in Coloma's story Ratón Pérez lives with his family in a biscuit box in the basement of the Prast confectionery in Madrid.
claims.statement_id: Ratu Maria Christina memesan cerita itu untuk Alfonso XIII yang baru tanggal giginya; dalam cerita Coloma, Ratón Pérez tinggal bersama keluarganya di kotak biskuit di ruang bawah tanah toko kue Prast di Madrid.
claims.quote: In 1894, Queen Maria Christina commissioned Coloma to write a tale for King Alfonso XIII, who had just lost a tooth at the age of eight. Coloma's story follows Ratón Pérez, who lived with his family in a box of cookies at the basement of Prast confectionery store in Madrid

claims.statement: He is usually called El Ratoncito Pérez, except in parts of Mexico, Guatemala, Peru and Chile, where he is El Ratón de los Dientes (the Tooth Mouse), and in Argentina, Venezuela, Uruguay and Colombia, where he is El Ratón Pérez.
claims.statement_id: Ia umumnya disebut El Ratoncito Pérez, kecuali di sebagian Meksiko, Guatemala, Peru, dan Chili, tempat ia disebut El Ratón de los Dientes (Tikus Gigi), dan di Argentina, Venezuela, Uruguay, dan Kolombia, tempat ia disebut El Ratón Pérez.
claims.quote: He is generally known as "El Ratoncito Pérez", except in some regions of Mexico, Guatemala, Peru and Chile, where he is called "El Ratón de los Dientes" ... The Tooth Mouse), and in Argentina, Venezuela, Uruguay and Colombia, where he is simply known as "El Ratón Pérez".

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, the most likely origin is the 18th-century French tale by Baroness d'Aulnoy, La Bonne Petite Souris.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, asal yang paling mungkin adalah dongeng Prancis abad ke-18 karya Baroness d'Aulnoy, La Bonne Petite Souris.
claims.quote: El origen más probable del ratoncito y su enlace con un hada proviene de un cuento francés del siglo XVIII de la baronesa d'Aulnoy: La Bonne Petite Souris (El buen ratoncito).

claims.statement: Elsewhere other beings collect teeth, such as the Tooth Fairy in Germanic countries, l'Angelet or La rateta in Catalonia and Maritxu teilatukoa in the Basque Country.
claims.statement_id: Di tempat lain ada makhluk pengumpul gigi lain, seperti Tooth Fairy di negara Jermanik, l'Angelet atau La rateta di Katalonia, dan Maritxu teilatukoa di negeri Basque.
claims.quote: En otros lugares hay otros seres fantásticos encargados de recoger los dientes, como Tooth Fairy («Hada de los dientes») en los países germanos, l'Angelet («el Angelito») o La rateta  («la Ratita») en Cataluña, Maritxu teilatukoa («Mari la del tejado») en el País Vasco

claims.statement: El Ratoncito Pérez stars in the 2006 Spanish-Argentine film The Hairy Tooth Fairy and its 2008 sequel.
claims.statement_id: Ratoncito Pérez dibintangi film Spanyol-Argentina The Hairy Tooth Fairy (2006) dan sekuelnya pada 2008.
claims.quote: El Ratoncito Pérez stars in the 2006 Spanish-Argentine film The Hairy Tooth Fairy and its 2008 sequel.

claims.statement: The Russian article also says he gives a child a present in exchange for a milk tooth placed under the pillow.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Rusia juga menyebut ia memberi hadiah sebagai ganti gigi susu yang ditaruh di bawah bantal.
claims.quote: По традиции дарит ребёнку подарок вместо выпавшего молочного зуба, положенного под подушку.

claims.statement: Akbuzat (Bashkir Aҡbuҙat; Tatar Akbuzat, 'light winged horse') is a figure of Turkic folklore and mythology, the totem ancestor of those peoples and a virtuous heroic horse.
claims.statement_id: Akbuzat (Bashkir: Aҡbuҙat; Tatar: Akbuzat, "kuda bersayap yang terang") adalah tokoh cerita rakyat dan mitologi Turkik, leluhur totem bangsa-bangsa itu dan kuda pahlawan yang luhur.
claims.quote: Akbuthat (bachkir : Aҡbuҙat ; tatar : Akbuzat  - cheval ailé léger) est un personnage du folklore et de la mythologie turque, l'ancêtre (ancêtre totem) de ces peuples, et vertu héroïque du cheval.

claims.statement: Akbuzat's origin is tied to widespread totemism among Turkic peoples and the cult of the horse, while white symbolises a safe birth, a happy life, a peaceful death and a worthy burial.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul Akbuzat terkait luasnya totemisme di kalangan bangsa Turkik dan pemujaan kuda, sedangkan warna putih melambangkan kelahiran yang selamat, hidup bahagia, kematian damai, dan pemakaman yang layak.
claims.quote: L'origine d'Akbuzat est liée à la large diffusion du totémisme parmi les peuples turciques, ainsi qu'au culte du cheval, qui jouait un rôle important dans la vie des Turcs. La couleur blanche symbolise une naissance réussie et heureuse, une vie, une mort paisible et un enterrement digne.

claims.statement: Tatar mythology tells of two divine heroic horses, Akbuzat and Kukbuzat (the sky-blue horse), who live in the sky, come down to help heroes, then return to the sky, tied to an iron stake.
claims.statement_id: Mitologi Tatar mengisahkan dua kuda pahlawan ilahi, Akbuzat dan Kukbuzat (kuda biru langit), yang hidup di langit, turun ke bumi membantu para pahlawan, lalu kembali ke langit dan ditambatkan pada tiang besi.
claims.quote: La mythologie tatare comprend l'histoire de deux chevaux héroïques divins, Akbuzat et Kukbuzat (cheval bleu ciel), vivant dans le ciel ; ces chevaux participent aux actions des héros, descendant sur terre, puis remontant au ciel, où ils sont attachés à un pieu de fer

claims.statement: According to the Russian article, the iron stake is Timerkazyk (the Pole Star) around which they graze, and seven horse thieves (the Great Bear) chase Akbuzat and Kukbuzat but can never catch them.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, tiang besi itu adalah Timerkazyk (Bintang Utara) tempat mereka merumput, dan tujuh pencuri kuda (Biduk) terus mengejar Akbuzat dan Kukbuzat tetapi tak pernah dapat menyusul.
claims.quote: где они привязаны к железному колу (тат. Тимерказык — Полярная звезда) и пасутся вокруг него. Семь конокрадов (Большая Медведица) преследуют Акбузата и Кукбузата, с целью похищения, но догнать не могут.

claims.statement: In Bashkir mythology it is a magic winged heroic horse, ancestor of the tulpars, Ural-Batyr's horse and the title character of the Bashkir epic (kubair) Akbuzat.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Bashkir ia kuda pahlawan bersayap yang ajaib, leluhur para tulpar, kuda Ural-Batyr, dan tokoh utama epos Bashkir (kubair) Akbuzat.
claims.quote: Dans la mythologie bachkire, c'est un cheval héroïque ailé magique, ancêtre des Tulpars. Cheval d'Oural-Batyr, personnage principal de l'épopée bachkire (kubair) « Akbuzat ».

claims.statement: According to the Bashkir article, it was born in the sky, can live on land and under water, does not burn in fire or sink in water, smashes mountains with its hooves and parts the sea.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Bashkir, ia lahir di langit, dapat hidup di darat dan di bawah air, tidak terbakar api, tidak tenggelam, menghancurkan gunung dengan kukunya, dan membelah laut.
claims.quote: Күктә тыуған, ерҙә һәм һыу аҫтында йәшәй ала, утта янмай, һыуҙа батмай, тояҡтары менән тауҙарҙы емерә һәм диңгеҙҙе айыра.

claims.statement: Akbuzat's mouth foam heals wounds when rubbed on them.
claims.statement_id: Busa mulut Akbuzat berkhasiat menyembuhkan luka bila dioleskan.
claims.quote: Аҡбуҙаттың ауыҙ күбеге шифалы — уны һөртөп, яраны бөтәштерәләр.

claims.statement: Antonio Spadavecchia with Kh. Zaimov wrote the opera Akbuzat ('The Magic Horse'), first staged in 1942 at the Bashkir State Opera and Ballet Theatre.
claims.statement_id: Antonio Spadavecchia bersama Kh. Zaimov menulis opera Akbuzat ("Kuda Ajaib") yang pertama dipentaskan pada 1942 di Teater Opera dan Balet Negara Bashkir.
claims.quote: Antonio Emmanuilovich Spadavecchia a écrit avec Kh. Zaimov l'opéra « Akbuzat » (« Le cheval magique »), créé pour la première fois en 1942 au Théâtre académique d'opéra et de ballet de l'État bachkir

claims.statement: In 2021 a five-metre monument (the horse itself 3.5 metres) cast at the Kasli foundry was set up in the Burzyansky district near Lake Yylkysykkan.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2021 di distrik Burzyansky dekat danau Yylkysykkan didirikan monumen setinggi lima meter (kudanya sendiri 3,5 meter) yang dicor di pengecoran Kasl.
claims.quote: En 2021, dans le district de Burzyansky, près du lac Yylkysykkan, un monument de cinq mètres de haut (le cheval lui-même y mesure 3,5 mètres) a été coulé à la fonderie de fer Kasl.

claims.statement: By legend the Bitard (or Outarde) is a mythical animal living in the forest of Ligugé near Poitiers, which gave its name to a student brotherhood, the Ordre du Vénéré Bitard, inspired by Rabelais.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Bitard (atau Outarde) adalah hewan mitis yang tinggal di hutan Ligugé dekat Poitiers, dan menjadi nama perkumpulan mahasiswa Ordre du Vénéré Bitard yang terilhami tulisan Rabelais.
claims.quote: Selon la légende, le Bitard (ou Outarde) serait un animal mythique qui vivrait dans la forêt de Ligugé près de Poitiers. Il a donné son nom à une confrérie étudiante, l'ordre du Vénéré Bitard, inspirée des écrits de Rabelais.

claims.statement: The Bitard is a chimeric, semi-divine creature with a marten's head, a carp's body, a hare's legs and peacock feathers, wearing academic palms round its neck.
claims.statement_id: Bitard adalah makhluk khimera setengah dewa berkepala musang, bertubuh ikan mas, berkaki kelinci, berbulu merak, dan berkalung palmes académiques.
claims.quote: Le Bitard est une créature chimérique, semi-divine, à tête de fouine, corps de carpe, pattes de lièvre, avec des plumes de paon. Il porte autour du cou des palmes académiques.

claims.statement: As first described, it has a marten's head, a salmon's body, a rump feathered with turkey plumes and a basset hound's legs.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran aslinya menyebut kepalanya dari musang, tubuhnya dari ikan salmon, bagian belakangnya berbulu kalkun, dan kakinya dari anjing basset.
claims.quote: Tel qu'il est décrit à l'origine : « le Bitard tient sa tête de la fouine, son corps du saumon, son derrière empenné de plumes de dindon, ses pattes du basset. »

claims.statement: The original tale tells how senior Poitiers students take newcomers into the woods to hunt the bitard with a sack and a light, until the newcomer is caught by a rural guard and fined for poaching.
claims.statement_id: Kisah aslinya menceritakan mahasiswa senior di Poitiers membawa mahasiswa baru ke hutan untuk memburu bitard dengan karung dan lampu, lalu mahasiswa baru itu tertangkap penjaga hutan dan harus membayar denda perburuan liar.
claims.quote: Le conte originel relate que, parmi les étudiants de Poitiers, des "anciens" accompagnent des jeunes dans les bois, à la recherche de cet animal mythique qu'est le bitard. Devant l'attirer dans un sac, avec une lumière, le jeune étudiant se fait surprendre par un garde-champêtre, et doit alors s'acquitter d'une amende pour braconnage...

claims.statement: The prank is also found outside student life, for example among servants welcoming newcomers, as recorded in the 1879 Bulletins of the statistical society of Deux-Sèvres.
claims.statement_id: Lelucon ini juga dikenal di luar dunia mahasiswa, misalnya di kalangan pembantu rumah tangga saat menyambut pendatang baru, seperti dicatat Bulletins de la Société de statistique du département des Deux-Sèvres tahun 1879.
claims.quote: On retrouve mention de cette farce hors du monde étudiant, par exemple chez des domestiques, lors de l'accueil de nouveaux, comme relaté dans les Bulletins de la Société de statistique du département des Deux-Sèvres de 1879.

claims.statement: It is the emblem of the Ordre du Vénéré Bitard, a student association of the University of Poitiers founded in the 1920s.
claims.statement_id: Bitard adalah lambang Ordre du Vénéré Bitard, perkumpulan mahasiswa Universitas Poitiers yang didirikan pada 1920-an.
claims.quote: It is the symbol of the Ordre du Vénéré Bitard (Loué Soit-Il !) or Order of the Venerated Bitard (May He be Blessed!), a student association of University of Poitiers (France) created in the 1920s.

claims.statement: The Order's lore refers to François Rabelais, since the word bitard appears twice among hunting spoils in Pantagruel.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi perkumpulan itu merujuk François Rabelais karena kata bitard muncul dua kali dalam hasil perburuan dalam Pantagruel.
claims.quote: The folklore of the Order refers to François Rabelais as the word bitard appears twice in hunting outcomes in Pantagruel.

claims.statement: The Spanish article calls the Bitard a legendary animal venerated by the Bitards.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Spanyol menyebut Bitard hewan legendaris yang dipuja para anggota perkumpulan Bitard.
claims.quote: El Bitardo es un animal legendario que los Bitardos veneran.

claims.statement: The same principle underlies the hunt for the Dahu (dahut).
claims.statement_id: Prinsip yang sama berlaku pada perburuan Dahu (dahut).
claims.quote: C'est le principe également de la chasse au dahut

claims.statement: In Manx folklore a buggane (or boagane) was a huge ogre-like creature native to the Isle of Man, which some consider akin to the Scandinavian troll.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Manx, buggane (atau boagane) adalah makhluk besar mirip raksasa pemakan manusia asli Pulau Man, yang oleh sebagian orang dianggap mirip troll Skandinavia.
claims.quote: In Manx folklore, a buggane (or boagane) was a huge ogre-like creature native to the Isle of Man. Some have considered them akin to the Scandinavian troll.

claims.statement: A malevolent shapeshifter, the buggane can appear as a large black calf or a human with a horse's ears or hooves, and is big enough to tear the roof off a church.
claims.statement_id: Buggane adalah pengubah wujud yang jahat, dapat muncul sebagai anak sapi hitam besar atau manusia bertelinga atau berkuku kuda, dan cukup besar untuk merobek atap gereja.
claims.quote: A shapeshifter, the buggane is generally described as a malevolent being that can appear as a large black calf or human with ears or hooves of a horse. It was large enough to tear the roof off a church.

claims.statement: Its natural form is 'covered with a mane of coarse, black hair; it had eyes like torches, and glittering sharp tusks'.
claims.statement_id: Wujud aslinya "tertutup surai rambut hitam kasar, bermata seperti obor, dan bertaring tajam berkilau".
claims.quote: Its natural form is described as "covered with a mane of coarse, black hair; it had eyes like torches, and glittering sharp tusks".

claims.statement: As magical creatures, bugganes could not cross water or stand on hallowed ground.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai makhluk gaib, buggane tidak dapat menyeberangi air atau berdiri di tanah suci.
claims.quote: As magical creatures, bugganes were unable to cross water or stand on hallowed ground.

claims.statement: The buggane's plan to wreck a ship was foiled by St Trinian, who guided it safely into Peel Harbour after the captain promised to build him a chapel.
claims.statement_id: Rencana buggane yang ingin mengandaskan kapal digagalkan Santo Trinian, yang menuntun kapal dengan selamat ke Pelabuhan Peel setelah sang kapten berjanji membangun kapel untuknya.
claims.quote: His plan was interdicted through the intervention of St. Trinian. Invoked by the captain with a promise to build a chapel in his honour, the saint guided the ship safely into Peel Harbour.

claims.statement: Enraged, the buggane cried that St Trinian should never have a whole church in Ellan Vannin; three times the people roofed the chapel and three times the buggane tore it off.
claims.statement_id: Marah, buggane berteriak bahwa Santo Trinian tidak akan pernah punya gereja utuh di Ellan Vannin; tiga kali warga memasang atap kapel, tiga kali pula buggane merobeknya.
claims.quote: Incensed, the buggane screamed, "St. Trinian should never have a whole church in Ellan Vannin." When the chapel came to be built, three times the local people put a roof on, and three times the buggane tore it off.

claims.statement: The fairies sometimes called on bugganes to punish those who offended them; the Glen Maye buggane would have thrown a lazy housewife into a waterfall for baking after sunset had she not cut her apron strings to escape.
claims.statement_id: Buggane kadang dipanggil para peri untuk menghukum orang yang menyinggung mereka; buggane Glen Maye nyaris melempar ibu rumah tangga yang malas ke air terjun karena memanggang setelah matahari terbenam, tetapi perempuan itu lolos dengan memotong tali celemeknya.
claims.quote: Bugganes were occasionally called upon by the fairies to punish people that had offended them. The buggane of Glen Maye would have pitched a lazy housewife into a waterfall for putting off baking until after sunset, had she not cut loose the strings of her apron to escape.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Irish legend says the Calf Sound south of the Isle of Man was formed in a fight between the Irish giant Finn Mac Cumaill and a buggane.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, legenda Irlandia menyebut selat Calf di selatan Pulau Man terbentuk dalam pertarungan antara raksasa Irlandia Finn Mac Cumaill dan seekor buggane.
claims.quote: Selon des légendes celtes irlandaises, le détroit de Calf, au sud de l'île de Man, fut créé au cours d'un combat entre le géant irlandais Finn Mac Cumaill et un buggane.

claims.statement: The Dutch article also calls the buggane a large ogre-like being of Manx mythology.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Belanda juga menyebut buggane makhluk besar mirip raksasa pemakan manusia dari mitologi Manx.
claims.quote: Een Buggane was in de Manx mythologie een groot Oger-achtig wezen, afkomstig van het Eiland Man.

claims.statement: The cuegle is a monster of Cantabrian folklore, two-legged and roughly humanlike, with black skin, a long beard, grey hair, three arms without hands or fingers, five rows of teeth, one stubby horn and three eyes: yellow, red and blue.
claims.statement_id: Cuegle adalah monster cerita rakyat Cantabria yang berjalan dengan dua kaki dan berwujud mirip manusia, berkulit hitam, berjanggut panjang, berambut kelabu, bertangan tiga tanpa telapak atau jari, bergigi lima baris, bertanduk satu yang pendek, dan bermata tiga: kuning, merah, dan biru.
claims.quote: The cuegle is a monster in Cantabrian folklore. Walking on two legs and roughly humanoid in shape, it is believed to have black skin, a long beard, grey hair, three arms without hands or fingers, five rows of teeth, a single stubby horn and three eyes in its head: one yellow, one red, and one blue.

claims.statement: Small as it is, it is very strong, attacks people and livestock and is said to steal babies from the cradle; oak or holly leaves, which repel it, protect the cradle.
claims.statement_id: Meski kecil ia sangat kuat, menyerang manusia dan ternak, dan konon mencuri bayi dari buaian; ia dapat ditangkal dengan daun ek atau holly, yang dibencinya, di buaian.
claims.quote: It is said to have great strength despite its small size.  The cuegle attacks people and livestock, and is reputed to steal babies from the cradle.  It may be protected against by placing oak or holly leaves, which it finds repulsive, in the cradle.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article the cuegle has one to three eyes, green, red and blue.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, cuegle bermata satu sampai tiga, berwarna hijau, merah, dan biru.
claims.quote: tiene la piel negra, una barba larga, pelo gris, tres brazos sin manos o dedos, cinco filas de dientes, un cuerno rechoncho y de uno a tres ojos en su cabeza. Uno verde, uno rojo y uno azul.

claims.statement: The cuegle can see past, present and future: the future with its forehead eye, the present with its right eye and the past with its left.
claims.statement_id: Cuegle dapat melihat masa lalu, kini, dan depan: masa depan dengan mata di dahi, masa kini dengan mata kanan, dan masa lalu dengan mata kiri.
claims.quote: El Cuegle puede ver cada uno, pasado, presente y futuro. El futuro lo ve con el ojo de la frente, el presente con el derecho y el pasado con el izquierdo.

claims.statement: The Catalan article also says babies can be protected by putting oak wood or holly leaves in the cradle.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Katalan juga menyebut bayi dapat dilindungi dengan kayu ek atau daun holly di buaian.
claims.quote: Els bebès poden ser protegits mitjançant la col·locació de fusta de roure o les fulles de grèvol, que propicien un efecte apotropaic, en el bressol.

claims.statement: The monster is referenced in the American TV series Grimm as a creature from Cantabria with three arms and three eyes.
claims.statement_id: Monster ini dirujuk dalam serial televisi Amerika Grimm sebagai makhluk dari Cantabria bertangan tiga dan bermata tiga.
claims.quote: En la sèrie de televisió americana Grimm es fa referència a aquest monstre, sent així, originari de la regió càntabra d'Espanya i posseint tres braços i tres ulls.

claims.statement: The moura encantada is a supernatural being of Portuguese and Galician fairy tales, very beautiful and seductive, living under an occult spell; shapeshifters, they haunt liminal places and are stone-builders of great strength.
claims.statement_id: Moura encantada adalah makhluk gaib dari dongeng Portugal dan Galisia, sangat cantik dan menggoda, hidup di bawah kutukan gaib; mereka pengubah wujud yang menghuni ruang ambang dan pembangun batu yang sangat kuat.
claims.quote: The Enchanted moura or moura encantada (enchanted female Mouros) is a supernatural being from the fairy tales of Portuguese and Galician folklore. Very beautiful and seductive, she lives under an imposed occult spell. Shapeshifters, the mouras encantadas occupy liminal spaces and are builders with stone of formidable strength.

claims.statement: According to the Portuguese article, they often appear singing and combing their long hair, golden or night-black, with a golden comb.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Portugis, mereka sering muncul bernyanyi sambil menyisir rambut panjangnya yang pirang seperti emas atau hitam seperti malam dengan sisir emas.
claims.quote: Aparecem frequentemente cantando e penteando os seus longos cabelos, louros como o ouro ou negros como a noite, com um pente de ouro

claims.statement: According to José Leite de Vasconcelos, they are beings forced by an occult power to live as if besieged, numb or asleep, until some circumstance breaks their spell.
claims.statement_id: Menurut José Leite de Vasconcelos, mereka makhluk yang dipaksa kekuatan gaib hidup seolah terkurung, kebas atau tertidur, selama suatu keadaan tertentu belum mematahkan kutukannya.
claims.quote: According to José Leite de Vasconcelos, mouras encantadas are “beings compelled by an occult power to live on a certain state of siege as if they were numb or asleep, insofar as a particular circumstance does not break  their spell".

claims.statement: By old lore they are the souls of maidens left guarding the treasures the male mouros encantados hid before leaving for Mourama.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita lama, mereka jiwa gadis-gadis yang ditinggalkan menjaga harta yang disembunyikan para mouros encantados sebelum pergi ke Mourama.
claims.quote: According to ancient lore, they are the souls of young maidens who were left guarding the treasures that the males, mouros encantados (enchanted mouros) hid before heading to Mourama.

claims.statement: Mouras encantadas are magical maidens who guard castles, caves, bridges, wells, fountains, rivers and treasures.
claims.statement_id: Mouras encantadas adalah gadis gaib penjaga kastel, gua, jembatan, sumur, mata air, sungai, dan harta.
claims.quote: Mouras encantadas are magical maidens who guard castles, caves, bridges, wells, fountains, rivers, and treasures.

claims.statement: Leite de Vasconcelos thought they may have absorbed the traits of local deities such as nymphs and nature spirits, and Consiglieri Pedroso called them 'feminine water genies'.
claims.statement_id: Leite de Vasconcelos menduga mereka menyerap ciri dewa setempat seperti nimfa dan roh alam, dan Consiglieri Pedroso menyebut mereka "jin air perempuan".
claims.quote: José Leite de Vasconcelos considered as a possibility that the mouras encantadas may have had assimilated the characteristics of local deities, such as nymphs and spirits of nature. Consiglieri Pedroso also referred to the mouras encantadas as "feminine water genies".

claims.statement: Tales of the mouras encantadas are thought to be of pre-Roman, Indo-European Celtic origin.
claims.statement_id: Dongeng tentang mereka dianggap berasal dari tradisi Kelt Indo-Eropa pra-Romawi.
claims.quote: The fairy tales featuring mouras encantadas are thought to be of pre-Roman, Indo-European Celtic origin.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, mouras are fairy beings of Galician and Portuguese folklore, whose male counterpart is the mouro.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, moura adalah makhluk peri dari cerita rakyat Galisia dan Portugal, dengan pasangan laki-laki bernama mouro.
claims.quote: Las mouras son criaturas fantásticas feéricas del folclore gallego y del folclore portugués de la península iberica. Su par masculino es el mouro.

claims.statement: According to the philologist Isodoro Millán, mouro (from Latin maurus) comes from Celtic mrvos, akin to Indo-European mr-tuos and Latin mortuus, so many authors hold the mouros were vanished races, the dead.
claims.statement_id: Menurut filolog Isodoro Millán, kata mouro (dari bahasa Latin maurus) berasal dari bahasa Kelt mrvos yang terkait istilah Indo-Eropa mr-tuos dan bahasa Latin mortuus, sehingga banyak penulis menganggap mouros ras yang telah punah, orang mati.
claims.quote: La voz latina maurus (de donde el gal. mouro) para el filólogo Isodoro Millán procede del celta mrvos afín al término indoeuropeo mr-tuos, que nos conduce al latín mortuus. De ahí que muchos autores sostengan que los mouros eran razas ya desaparecidas, muertos.

claims.statement: The fish-man of Liérganes (El hombre pez) is a figure of Cantabrian mythology, an amphibious humanlike being that seemed the transformation of a real man lost at sea.
claims.statement_id: Manusia ikan Liérganes (El hombre pez) adalah sosok mitologi Cantabria, makhluk amfibi berwujud manusia yang tampak seperti hasil perubahan seorang manusia nyata yang hilang di laut.
claims.quote: The fish-man of Liérganes (Spanish: El hombre pez) is an entity of the mythology of Cantabria, located in the north of Spain. The fish-man would be an amphibian human-looking being, who looked a lot like a metamorphosis of a real human being who was lost at sea.

claims.statement: His story was examined by the Enlightenment writer Benito Jerónimo Feijoo, who claimed it was true.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya diselidiki penulis Pencerahan Benito Jerónimo Feijoo, yang menyatakan kisah itu benar.
claims.quote: His story was examined by Enlightenment writer Benito Jerónimo Feijoo, who claimed that the story was true.

claims.statement: According to Feijoo, Francisco de la Vega Casar of Liérganes worked as a carpenter in Bilbao until 1674, when on St John's Eve he went swimming with friends in the Bilbao estuary.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Feijoo, Francisco de la Vega Casar dari Liérganes bekerja sebagai tukang kayu di Bilbao sampai 1674, ketika pada malam Santo Yohanes ia berenang bersama teman-temannya di muara Bilbao.
claims.quote: This son, who according to Feijoo was called Francisco de la Vega Casar, lived in Bilbao as a carpenter till 1674 when, on Saint John's Day Eve, he went with some friends to swim in Bilbao's estuary.

claims.statement: He was last seen swimming out to sea and was thought drowned.
claims.statement_id: Ia terakhir terlihat berenang menjauh ke laut dan dianggap tenggelam.
claims.quote: He was last seen swimming away into the sea, and it was thought that he had drowned.

claims.statement: Five years later, in 1679, fishermen in the Bay of Cádiz saw a strange creature caught in their nets, struggling to escape.
claims.statement_id: Lima tahun kemudian, pada 1679, nelayan di Teluk Cádiz melihat makhluk aneh tersangkut di jaring mereka dan berusaha meloloskan diri.
claims.quote: However, five years later, in 1679, while some fishers were seafaring in the Bay of Cadiz, in southern Spain, they noticed that a strange-looking creature had become entangled with their fishing nets, and was trying to fight its way out.

claims.statement: Once caught with bread, the creature proved to be a young man with white skin and thin red hair, but with a strip of scales from throat to belly and down his spine, and what looked like gills on his neck.
claims.statement_id: Setelah ditangkap dengan umpan roti, makhluk itu ternyata berwujud pemuda berkulit putih berambut merah tipis, tetapi bersisik dari leher sampai perut dan di sepanjang tulang punggung, serta tampak berinsang di lehernya.
claims.quote: When they got the creature on board, they found that it had indeed a human shape: it looked like a young man, with white skin and thin red hair. However, he also showed some fish-like signs, such as a strip of scales that went down from his throat to his stomach, another one that covered his spine, and what seemingly were gills around his neck.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, the first account of the fish-man is in volume VI of Fray Benito Jerónimo Feijoo's Teatro crítico universal.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, catatan pertama kisah manusia ikan ada dalam jilid VI Teatro crítico universal karya Fray Benito Jerónimo Feijoo.
claims.quote: La primera reseña en la que aparece el relato del hombre pez es en el volumen VI del Teatro crítico universal de Fray Benito Jerónimo Feijoo.

claims.statement: José María Herrán later wrote the book El hombre-pez de Liérganes (Santander, 1877), and there is now an interpretation centre in an old mill at Liérganes.
claims.statement_id: José María Herrán kemudian menulis buku El hombre-pez de Liérganes (Santander, 1877), dan kini ada pusat informasi tentangnya di bekas penggilingan di Liérganes.
claims.quote: Posteriormente José María Herrán escribió un libro titulado El hombre-pez de Liérganes (Santander, 1877), basado en esta historia tradicional popular. Actualmente existe un centro de interpretación en Liérganes, emplazado en un antiguo molino

claims.statement: The Russian article says the fish-man statue on the bank of the Miera became one of Liérganes' main sights.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Rusia menyebut patung manusia ikan di tepi Sungai Miera menjadi salah satu daya tarik utama Liérganes.
claims.quote: Позднее, статуя человека-рыбы, установленная на берегу Мьеры, стала одной из основных достопримечательностей Льерганеса.

claims.statement: In Nordic folklore, genganger (Danish), gjenganger (Norwegian) or gengångare (Swedish), 'again-walker', is a term for a revenant or ghost.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Nordik, genganger (Denmark), gjenganger (Norwegia), atau gengångare (Swedia), "yang berjalan lagi", adalah sebutan untuk mayat hidup atau hantu.
claims.quote: In Nordic folklore; Danish: genganger, Norwegian: gjenganger, Swedish: gengångare ("(a)gain-walker"), among more, is a term for a revenant or ghost, meaning "someone which goes again"

claims.statement: Other forms are Icelandic afturganga and Norwegian attergangar from Old Norse aptrgangr, and Danish genfærd and Norwegian gjenferd.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk lain adalah afturganga (Islandia) dan attergangar (Norwegia) dari bahasa Norse Kuno aptrgangr, serta genfærd (Denmark) dan gjenferd (Norwegia).
claims.quote: Other forms includes Icelandic: afturganga, Norwegian: attergangar, stemming from Old Norse: aptrgangr ("re-walker"); Danish: genfærd, Norwegian: gjenferd ("again-travel or after-journey").

claims.statement: A gjenganger might return from the afterlife for several reasons: the murdered and their murderers seldom rested in their graves, and suicides often came back as gjengangere.
claims.statement_id: Gjenganger kembali dari alam baka karena berbagai sebab: korban dan pembunuhnya jarang tenang di kubur, dan orang yang bunuh diri sering kembali sebagai gjengangere.
claims.quote: A gjenganger could have several reasons to return from the afterlife. Murdered people and their murderers could seldom sleep peacefully in their graves. People who had committed suicide often came back as gjengangere.

claims.statement: Others came back because they had left something undone, and usually needed someone's help before they could rest.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula yang kembali karena meninggalkan urusan yang belum selesai, dan biasanya mereka membutuhkan bantuan seseorang sebelum akhirnya tenang.
claims.quote: At other times, people came back from the grave because they had left something undone. Most often they needed someone to help them do this, before they could finally be at peace.

claims.statement: In Scandinavian tradition the gjenganger had an entirely bodily form and usually no ghostly qualities at all.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Skandinavia, gjenganger berwujud sepenuhnya jasmani dan biasanya sama sekali tidak seperti hantu.
claims.quote: The gjenganger in the Scandinavian tradition took on an entirely corporeal form. It normally had no spectre-like qualities whatsoever.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the creature seems to come from Norse mythology, since such beings already appear in medieval Icelandic sagas such as Grettis saga, Eyrbyggja saga and the saga of Erik the Red.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, makhluk ini tampaknya berasal dari mitologi Nordik karena sudah disebut dalam saga Islandia abad pertengahan seperti saga Grettis, saga Eyrbyggja, dan saga Erik si Merah.
claims.quote: Cette créature semble originaire de la mythologie nordique, puisque de telles créatures sont déjà citées dans certaines sagas islandaises médiévales, à l'exemple de la saga Grettis, la saga Eyrbyggja ou la saga d'Erik le Rouge.

claims.statement: The Italian article calls the gjenganger a revenant of Scandinavian folklore, a ghost returned from the grave.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Italia menyebut gjenganger revenant dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, hantu yang kembali dari kubur.
claims.quote: Un Gjenganger (in Norvegese: Gjenganger, Attergangar o Gjenferd; in lingua danese: Genganger o Genfærd; in svedese: Gengångare) è un revenant del folclore scandinavo, un fantasma tornato dalla tomba.

claims.statement: The hercinia is a legendary bird with glowing feathers that lived in the Hercynian Forest of ancient Germany.
claims.statement_id: Hercinia adalah burung legendaris berbulu bercahaya yang menghuni Hutan Hercynia di Germania kuno.
claims.quote: Hercinia is a legendary bird with glowing feathers that inhabited the Hercynian Forest of ancient Germany.

claims.statement: The hercinia appears in Medieval bestiaries and was recorded in the 1st century by Pliny the Elder: 'In the Hercynian Forest, in Germany, we hear of a singular kind of bird, the feathers of which shine at night like fire.'
claims.statement_id: Hercinia digambarkan dalam bestiari Abad Pertengahan dan dicatat pada abad ke-1 oleh Plinius Tua: "Di Hutan Hercynia, di Germania, terdengar kabar tentang sejenis burung aneh yang bulunya bersinar seperti api pada malam hari."
claims.quote: The hercinia is depicted in Medieval bestiaries and was recorded in the 1st century by Pliny the Elder, who wrote, "In the Hercynian Forest, in Germany, we hear of a singular kind of bird, the feathers of which shine at night like fire".

claims.statement: Writing in the 7th century, Isidore of Seville notes that its feathers sparkle so that, however dark the night, feathers laid on the ground give off light that marks the path.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-7 Isidorus dari Sevilla menulis bahwa bulunya begitu berkilau sehingga, segelap apa pun malam, bulu yang diletakkan di tanah memancarkan cahaya penunjuk jalan.
claims.quote: Writing in the 7th century, Isidore of Seville notes, "Their feathers sparkle so much in the shade that, however dark the night is with thick shadows, these feathers, when placed on the ground, give off light that helps to mark the way, and the sign of the glittering feathers makes clear the direction of the path".

claims.statement: Reports of the hercinia may come from birds with iridescent feathers reflecting moonlight, as reported of several species including the barn owl and the bittern.
claims.statement_id: Laporan tentang hercinia mungkin berasal dari burung berbulu warna-warni yang memantulkan cahaya bulan, gejala yang dilaporkan pada beberapa spesies seperti burung hantu serak dan burung bittern.
claims.quote: It is possible that the reports of the hercinia were based on sightings of birds with iridescent feathers that reflected moonlight, a phenomenon that has been reported of a number of species of birds, including the barn owl and the bittern.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the legend inspired many works of art, notably Thomas Moore's poem A Dream of Antiquity.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, legenda burung bercahaya ini mengilhami banyak karya seni, termasuk puisi Thomas Moore A Dream of Antiquity.
claims.quote: La légende de ces oiseaux lumineux présents dans la forêt Hercynienne a inspiré de nombreuses œuvres d’art, notamment le célèbre poème de Thomas Moore : A Dream of Antiquity.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, they lived in the Hercynian Forest in southern Germany, where their glowing feathers lit the paths through the thick forest.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, burung-burung ini tinggal di Hutan Hercynia di Jerman selatan, tempat bulu bercahayanya menerangi jalan setapak di hutan lebat.
claims.quote: Ellos se encontraban en el bosque Hercínico, en el sur de Alemania, donde sus plumas brillantes mantenían sendas encendidas en la espesura del bosque.

claims.statement: Inguma (Mauma in Baigorri) is the god of dreams in Basque mythology and religion, a malevolent force that enters houses at night and torments the residents with nightmares, sometimes killing them.
claims.statement_id: Inguma (Mauma di Baigorri) adalah dewa mimpi dalam mitologi dan agama Basque, kekuatan jahat yang masuk ke rumah pada malam hari dan menyiksa penghuni dengan mimpi buruk, kadang sampai membunuh mereka.
claims.quote: Inguma (Mauma in Baigorri) is the god of dreams in Basque mythology and religion.  He is regarded as a malevolent force who enters houses at night and plagues residents with nightmares, sometimes killing them.

claims.statement: He is mentioned in Ofrenda a la tormenta, the third film of Dolores Redondo's Baztán trilogy.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut dalam Ofrenda a la tormenta, film ketiga trilogi Baztán karya Dolores Redondo.
claims.quote: He is mentioned in Ofrenda a la tormenta (Offering to the Storm), the third film in the Baztán trilogy by Dolores Redondo.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Inguma is one of the irelus or evil spirits of the wide Basque pantheon.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Inguma adalah salah satu irelu atau roh jahat dalam jajaran makhluk mitologi Basque.
claims.quote: Inguma, ou Mauma à Baigorri, est un des Irelus ou génies maléfiques qui composent le vaste panthéon de la mythologie basque.

claims.statement: His nature is evil, his only aim to choke his victims in their sleep: he appears in houses at night and squeezes sleepers' throats, making breathing hard and causing unspeakable dread.
claims.statement_id: Sifatnya jahat karena tujuannya hanya mencekik korbannya saat tidur: ia muncul di rumah pada malam hari dan mencekik leher orang yang tidur sehingga sulit bernapas dan sangat ketakutan.
claims.quote: Sa nature est mauvaise, puisque son seul but est de noyer ses victimes pendant leur sommeil. Il apparaît de nuit dans les maisons, lorsque les gens sont endormis. Il serre la gorge de certains d'entre eux, leur rendant la respiration difficile, provoquant ainsi une indicible angoisse.

claims.statement: The anthropological origin of this spirit may lie in sleep paralysis.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul antropologis roh ini mungkin terletak pada kelumpuhan tidur.
claims.quote: L'origine anthropologique de ce génie pourrait être recherchée dans le phénomène appelé « paralysie du sommeil »

claims.statement: Inguma sits on his victims' chests and squeezes their throats with his hands.
claims.statement_id: Inguma duduk di dada korbannya dan mencekik leher mereka dengan tangannya.
claims.quote: ce qui coïncide avec le schéma suivi par Inguma, qui s'assoit sur la poitrine de ses victimes et leur serre la gorge avec ses mains.

claims.statement: According to the Polish article, the protection against this demon was a prayer to St Andrew and St Agnes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Polandia, perlindungan terhadap iblis ini adalah doa kepada Santo Andreas dan Santa Agnes.
claims.quote: Ochroną przed demonem była modllitwa do św. Andrzeja i św. Agnieszki.

claims.statement: He was sometimes identified with the demon Aideko.
claims.statement_id: Kadang ia disamakan dengan iblis Aideko.
claims.quote: Czasami utożsamiano go z demonem Aideko.

claims.statement: San Martin Txiki ('Little Saint Martin') is the trickster of Basque mythology; txiki means 'little' in an affectionate sense.
claims.statement_id: San Martin Txiki ("Santo Martin Kecil") adalah tokoh penipu cerdik dalam mitologi Basque; txiki berarti "kecil" dalam arti sayang.
claims.quote: San Martin Txiki ("Little Saint Martin") is the trickster figure from Basque mythology. Txiki (pronounced "cheeky" [ˈt͡ʃiːki]) means "little" in an affectionate sense.

claims.statement: He stole the secrets of planting, sowing and harvesting from the Basajaunak (lords of the woods), and invented the first saws on the model of the chestnut leaf's edge.
claims.statement_id: Ia mencuri rahasia menanam, menabur, dan memanen dari Basajaunak (penguasa hutan), dan menciptakan gergaji pertama meniru tepi daun kastanye.
claims.quote: He stole the secrets of planting, sowing, and harvesting from the Basajaunak (lords of the woods). He also invented the first saws, modeling them after the edges of the chestnut leaf.

claims.statement: San Martin Txiki also exists in Aragonese mythology in the Tena, Ansó and Broto valleys as San Martinico.
claims.statement_id: San Martin Txiki juga ada dalam mitologi Aragon di lembah Tena, Ansó, dan Broto dengan nama San Martinico.
claims.quote: San Martin Txiki also exists in Aragonese mythology in the valleys of Tena, Ansó and Broto (places where local toponymy derives from Basque) under the name San Martinico.

claims.statement: The Basajaunak kept all the wheat for themselves, so San Martin Txiki bet them he could jump a pile of wheat seed without touching it.
claims.statement_id: Basajaunak menyimpan semua gandum untuk diri mereka, lalu San Martin Txiki bertaruh bahwa ia bisa melompati tumpukan benih gandum tanpa menyentuhnya.
claims.quote: It is said that the Basajaunak kept all the wheat for themselves, so San Martin Txiki bet them that he could he could jump over a pile of wheat seeds without touching it.

claims.statement: He fell in on purpose wearing big shoes, so wheat seeds collected in them; the Basajaunak, busy laughing, did not notice, and he brought the seeds to humans.
claims.statement_id: Ia sengaja jatuh ke tumpukan itu dengan memakai sepatu besar sehingga benih gandum masuk ke sepatunya; Basajaunak sibuk menertawakannya dan tidak sadar, lalu ia membawa benih itu kepada manusia.
claims.quote: However, he had worn large shoes that day, and collected some wheat seeds in them when he fell in. The Basajaunak were so busy laughing at him that they didn't notice, and he brought the seeds back to the humans.

claims.statement: He got the saw through his servant: the Basajaunak asked whether he had been inspired by chestnut leaves, and from that San Martin Txiki made one himself.
claims.statement_id: Rahasia gergaji ia dapat lewat pelayannya: Basajaunak bertanya apakah ia terilhami daun kastanye, dan dari situ San Martin Txiki membuat gergajinya sendiri.
claims.quote: The Basajaunak asked his servant if he had been inspired by the shape of chestnut leaves. The servant told him what they had said, and San Martin Txiki was then able to make one himself.

claims.statement: According to the French article, Martin Txiki, Martintxo or San Martiniko is seen as the civilising hero of the Basque people, his name a transformation of St Martin of Tours.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Martin Txiki, Martintxo, atau San Martiniko dianggap pahlawan pembawa peradaban bagi bangsa Basque, dan namanya berasal dari Santo Martinus dari Tours.
claims.quote: Martin txiki (Martin le petit), Martintxo, San Martin txiki (saint Martin le petit) ou San Martiniko est considéré comme le héros « civilisateur » du peuple basque. Ce nom est une transformation de celui de saint Martin, un saint tourangeau qui figure dans un thème légendaire.

claims.statement: In the Ataun version a Basajaun who noticed the theft threw an axe, which missed and stuck in a chestnut trunk at Mekolalde, San Gregorio d'Ataun.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Ataun, seorang Basajaun yang menyadari pencurian itu melemparkan kapak, tetapi meleset dan menancap di batang kastanye di Mekolalde, San Gregorio d'Ataun.
claims.quote: Il lança dans sa direction son arme de jet, une hache. Ratant Martín Txiki, celle-ci se planta dans le tronc d'un châtaignier, au lieu-dit Mekolalde à San Gregorio d'Ataun

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, this trickster was probably created by popular imagination as an archetype of the Celtiberian healers of the Moncayo area who travelled to Basque and Pyrenean lands with bronze, copper and iron tools.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, tokoh penipu ini mungkin diciptakan imajinasi rakyat sebagai arketipe tabib Keltiberia dari daerah Moncayo yang berkelana ke negeri Basque dan Pyrenees dengan perkakas perunggu, tembaga, dan besi.
claims.quote: Este trickster probablemente lo creara la imaginación popular como arquetipo de los sanadores celtibéricos de la zona del Moncayo (más en concreto de los de San Martín de la Virgen de Moncayo), que viajaban a tierras vasconas y/o pirenaicas a curar a los enfermos con herramientas de bronce, cobre y hierro

claims.statement: In folklore the Michigan Dogman is an alleged creature first seen in 1887 in Wexford County, Michigan, United States, described as a seven-foot (2.1 m), blue- or amber-eyed two-legged canine with a man's torso and a howl like a human scream.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat, Michigan Dogman adalah makhluk yang konon pertama terlihat pada 1887 di Wexford County, Michigan, Amerika Serikat, digambarkan sebagai anjing berkaki dua setinggi tujuh kaki (2,1 m) bermata biru atau kuning, bertubuh manusia, dengan lolongan seperti jeritan manusia.
claims.quote: In folklore, the Michigan Dogman is an alleged creature first witnessed in 1887 in Wexford County, Michigan, United States. It was described as a seven-foot-tall (2.1 m), blue- or amber-eyed bipedal canid possessing the torso of a man with a fearsome howl resembling a human scream.

claims.statement: Folklore says the creature reappears every ten years, in years ending in seven.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, makhluk ini muncul kembali setiap sepuluh tahun pada tahun yang berakhiran angka tujuh.
claims.quote: Folklore claims that the creature reemerges on a recurring ten-year pattern linked to years ending in the number seven.

claims.statement: In 1987 disc jockey Steve Cook of WTCM-FM in Traverse City recorded a song, The Legend, first played as an April Fool's joke.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1987 penyiar radio Steve Cook di WTCM-FM, Traverse City, merekam lagu The Legend yang mula-mula diputar sebagai lelucon April Mop.
claims.quote: In 1987, disc jockey Steve Cook at WTCM-FM in Traverse City, Michigan, recorded a song titled "The Legend", which he initially played as an April Fool's Day joke.

claims.statement: Cook said he made it up entirely from his own imagination as an April Fools' prank for the radio.
claims.statement_id: Cook mengaku mengarang lagu itu sepenuhnya dari imajinasinya sebagai lelucon April Mop untuk radio.
claims.quote: I made it up completely from my own imagination as an April Fools' prank for the radio and stumbled my way to a legend that goes back all the way to Native American times.

claims.statement: After he played the song, Cook got calls from listeners who said they had met a similar creature.
claims.statement_id: Setelah lagu itu diputar, Cook menerima telepon dari pendengar yang mengaku pernah bertemu makhluk serupa.
claims.quote: After he played the song, Cook received calls from listeners who said that they had encountered a similar creature.

claims.statement: According to the French article, the Dogman is a two-legged dog-like animal of Michigan folklore born of a 1987 local song, possibly echoing older tales.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Dogman adalah hewan berkaki dua mirip anjing dari cerita rakyat Michigan yang lahir dari lagu lokal tahun 1987, mungkin menggemakan cerita yang lebih tua.
claims.quote: L'Homme chien du Michigan (Dogman of Michigan) animal bipède ressemblant à un canidé issu du folklore du Michigan et née d'une chanson locale sortie en 1987 faisant potentiellement écho à des récits plus anciens.

claims.statement: According to Cook a Native legend has the dogman roaming the Manistee River since Odawa times, though no authentic source has ever been documented.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cook ada legenda penduduk asli bahwa makhluk ini berkeliaran di sekitar Sungai Manistee sejak zaman suku Odawa, tetapi tidak ada sumber autentik yang pernah terdokumentasi.
claims.quote: Selon Cook, une légende amérindienne existerait, ce qui fait dire que l'homme chien rode autour de la rivière Manistee depuis l'époque où les tribus Odawa y vivaient bien qu'aucune source authentique n'ait jamais été documentée.

claims.statement: According to the Russian article, cryptozoological literature classes the dogman as an alleged upright canid, while folklorists see it mainly as a figure of modern regional legend.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Rusia, literatur kriptozoologi menggolongkannya makhluk mirip anjing yang berjalan tegak, sedangkan para folkloris memandangnya terutama sebagai tokoh legenda regional modern.
claims.quote: В криптозоологической литературе догмена относят к предполагаемым прямоходящим псовоподобным существам, тогда как фольклористы рассматривают его прежде всего как персонажа современной региональной легенды.

claims.statement: In Catalan mythology the Muladona or Donamula ('mule-woman') is a female mule with a woman's head; by legend a young woman cursed by her townsfolk for being irreverent and irreligious was turned into a mule.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Katalan, Muladona atau Donamula ("bagal-perempuan") adalah bagal betina berkepala perempuan; menurut legenda, seorang gadis yang tidak hormat dan tidak beragama dikutuk warga desanya menjadi bagal.
claims.quote: In Catalan mythology, a Muladona or Donamula (mule-woman or woman-mule in Catalan) is a female mule with a human woman's head. Legend has it that a young woman was cursed by the townspeople for being irreverent and irreligious, and the curse turned her into a mule.

claims.statement: She roamed the mountains, especially at night, joining mule trains, whose mules were so frightened they stampeded into ravines and died.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkeliaran di pegunungan, terutama malam hari, dan bergabung dengan rombongan bagal, yang ketakutan hingga berlari ke jurang dan mati.
claims.quote: According to legend, she wandered mountains, especially at night, joining mule trains. It was claimed that mules were frightened by her presence enough to stampede into ravines and die.

claims.statement: The Muladona looks like a mule but is a mix of human and animal: her mane is like a woman's hair, and her face, though animal-like, is clearly human.
claims.statement_id: Muladona tampak seperti bagal tetapi campuran manusia dan hewan: surainya seperti rambut perempuan dan wajahnya, walau seperti hewan, jelas manusia.
claims.quote: The Muladona looks like a mule, but it is a mixture of human and animal, its mane is like a woman's hair and its face, while still appearing to be like that of an animal, is obviously human.

claims.statement: She is always shown with a mule's four legs, sometimes with the front legs joined to a chest where a mule's neck would be, and always with breasts to stress she is female.
claims.statement_id: Ia selalu digambarkan berkaki empat bagal, kadang dengan kaki depan menyatu pada dada manusia di tempat leher bagal, dan selalu berpayudara untuk menegaskan bahwa ia perempuan.
claims.quote: It is always represented with the four legs of a mule, but sometimes the front two legs join a thorax, located where a mule would have its neck. In addition, the animal is always represented with breasts to underline that it is female.

claims.statement: Muleteers fed their mules little Muladona-shaped breads so the animals would not take fright and would ignore her if she appeared.
claims.statement_id: Para kusir bagal memberi bagal mereka roti kecil berbentuk Muladona agar hewan itu tidak takut dan mengabaikannya bila ia muncul.
claims.quote: The muleteers used to give their mules small Muladona-shaped pieces of bread to eat, in the belief that this would stop the animals being frightened and allow them to ignore her if she appeared.

claims.statement: According to the Spanish article, during the journey they kept counting their animals so the Muladona would not slip in among them unnoticed.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, selama perjalanan mereka terus menghitung bagal agar Muladona tidak menyusup tanpa ketahuan.
claims.quote: Así y todo, durante la marcha contaban las cabezas que llevaban para evitar que la muladona se hubiese mezclado con sus animales sin que ellos se diesen cuenta y acabasen pagándolo caro.

claims.statement: The Assamese article also calls the Muladona a female mule with a woman's head in Catalan mythology.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Assam juga menyebut Muladona bagal betina berkepala perempuan dalam mitologi Katalan.
claims.quote: কাটালন পৌৰাণিক কাহিনীত মুলাডোনা বা ডোনামুলা বুলিও কোৱা (কাটালান ভাষাত খচ্চৰ-মহিলা বা মহিলা-খচ্চৰ) হৈছে মানৱ নাৰীৰ মূৰ থকা এটা মাইকী খচ্চৰ।

claims.statement: In folklore a revenant is a spirit or animated corpse believed to have risen to haunt the living; the word comes from Old French revenant, 'returning'.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat, revenant adalah roh atau mayat hidup yang dipercaya bangkit untuk menghantui orang hidup; kata revenant berasal dari bahasa Prancis Kuno, "yang kembali".
claims.quote: In folklore, a revenant is a spirit or animated corpse that is believed to have been resurrected to haunt the living. The word revenant is derived from the Old French word revenant 'returning' (see also the related French verb revenir 'to come back').

claims.statement: Revenants feature in the legends of various cultures, including Celtic and Norse mythology, and tales of revenant visits were recorded by English historians in the Middle Ages.
claims.statement_id: Revenant ada dalam legenda berbagai budaya, termasuk mitologi Kelt dan Norse, dan kisah kunjungan revenant dicatat sejarawan Inggris pada Abad Pertengahan.
claims.quote: Revenants are part of the legend of various cultures, including Celtic and Norse mythology, and stories of supposed revenant visitations were documented by English historians in the Middle Ages.

claims.statement: Archaeologists have found revenant graves across Europe, with bodies given precautions against rising, such as stones on the legs, stones in the jaw so it could not speak, bodies wedged with bricks or body parts removed.
claims.statement_id: Arkeolog menemukan kuburan revenant di seluruh Eropa, berisi jasad yang diberi pencegahan agar tidak bangkit, seperti batu di atas kaki, batu di rahang agar tak bisa bicara, jasad yang diganjal bata, atau bagian tubuh yang dibuang.
claims.quote: Archaeologists have found revenant graves throughout Europe, characterized by bodies that had precautions taken to prevent them from rising up and causing mischief for the living, such as stones placed over the legs, stones placed in the jaw so it could not speak, bodies lodged with bricks, or body parts removed.

claims.statement: The oldest known graves date to about 4,000 years BP in the Bronze Age; Roman literature wrote of revenants, they were common through the Middle Ages, and 17th-century Poland was reportedly a hotbed of the belief.
claims.statement_id: Kuburan tertua berasal dari sekitar 4.000 tahun lalu pada Zaman Perunggu; sastra Romawi menulis tentang revenant, kepercayaan ini umum sepanjang Abad Pertengahan, dan Polandia abad ke-17 konon menjadi pusatnya.
claims.quote: The oldest known graves are as old as 4,000 years BP from the Bronze Age. Roman literature contained writings about revenants. They were common throughout the Middle Ages, and 17th-century Poland was reportedly a hot-bed of revenant superstition.

claims.statement: Folklorists have used 'revenant' interchangeably with 'ghost'; some say vampires come from Eastern and revenants from Western European folklore, but many hold revenant is a general term for the undead.
claims.statement_id: Folkloris memakai istilah revenant bergantian dengan hantu; sebagian berpendapat vampir berasal dari Eropa Timur dan revenant dari Eropa Barat, tetapi banyak yang menganggap revenant istilah umum untuk mayat hidup.
claims.quote: The term "revenant" has been used interchangeably with "ghost" by folklorists. While some maintain that vampires derive from Eastern European folklore and revenants derive from Western European folklore, many assert that revenant is a generic term for the undead.

claims.statement: Augustin Calmet researched the subject at length in his Traité sur les apparitions des esprits et sur les vampires ou les revenans de Hongrie, de Moravie (1751).
claims.statement_id: Augustin Calmet meneliti topik ini secara luas dalam Traité sur les apparitions des esprits et sur les vampires ou les revenans de Hongrie, de Moravie (1751).
claims.quote: Augustin Calmet conducted extensive research on the topic in his work titled Traité sur les apparitions des esprits et sur les vampires ou les revenans de Hongrie, de Moravie, &c. (1751) in which he describes the related rumors of the time.

claims.statement: The Portuguese article also calls the revenant a spirit or animated corpse believed revived from death to haunt the living.
claims.statement_id: Artikel bahasa Portugis juga menyebut revenant roh atau mayat hidup yang dipercaya bangkit dari kematian untuk menghantui orang hidup.
claims.quote: No folclore, um revenant ou revenã é um espírito ou cadáver animado, em que se acredita ter sido revivido da morte para assombrar os vivos.

claims.statement: According to the Czech article, a revenant is a revived dead body that comes into contact with the living, the word from Latin revenire, 'to return'.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel bahasa Ceko, revenant adalah jasad mati yang hidup kembali dan berhubungan dengan orang hidup, dan katanya dari bahasa Latin revenire, "kembali".
claims.quote: Revenant je v mytologii a folklóru oživené mrtvé tělo, které přichází do kontaktu s živými. Slovo je odvozeno od latinského revenire („navracet se“)

claims.statement: The belief that an unusual death causes wandering after death is widespread among Indo-Europeans.
claims.statement_id: Keyakinan bahwa kematian yang tidak wajar menyebabkan arwah mengembara setelah mati tersebar luas di kalangan bangsa Indo-Eropa.
claims.quote: Přesvědčení, že neobvyklá smrt je příčinou posmrtného bloudění, je u Indoevropanů obecně rozšířena.

claims.statement: The squasc is a mythological being of eastern Lombardy folklore.
claims.statement_id: Squasc adalah makhluk mitologis dalam cerita rakyat Lombardia timur.
claims.quote: The squasc ... is a mythological being of the Eastern Lombardy region folklore.

claims.statement: According to the Italian article it is a small, hairy, tawny being like a tailless squirrel but with a human face.
